people.summary: Maria Donata's father, who lived in San Bartolomeo in Galdo and had died by January 1884. He is known from a single line in his daughter's marriage act.
people.story:
Giuseppe Circelli is known from one line. When his daughter Maria Donata married in January 1884, the clerk recorded her as the daughter "del fu Giuseppe", the late Giuseppe, who had lived in the town during his lifetime.[^marriage-1884] By then he was dead, and so was his wife.

Because neither parent was alive, the act records that consent to the marriage came from the bride's family council, the consiglio di famiglia, a group of relatives who stood in for parents who had died.[^marriage-1884]

That is all the records in this collection say about him. His age, his trade and his date of death are not known. Circelli was a common surname in San Bartolomeo in Galdo, and the town's civil registers survive on the Antenati portal, so his death record, and perhaps his marriage, should be findable there.[^research-md]

Update, November 2026. Giuseppe's own story now begins in the town's oldest civil registers. He was twenty-three, a farmer, when he promised himself in marriage to Anna Rita Mansolino on 17 January 1850; the clerk noted that his parents, Donato Circelli and Vincenza, had both died.[^marriage-circelli-mansolino-1850] On 3 January 1860 he registered twin daughters, Maria Filomena and Maria Lucia, and on 25 September 1863, at ten in the morning, he brought his new daughter Maria Donata to be recorded. She was baptized that same day.[^birth-circelli-twins-1860][^birth-maria-donata-1863]

Update, November 2026: his own birth act has now been found. On 13 February 1827 his father, Donato Circelli, a farm worker of forty-two from Strada Borgo Nuovo, came to the town hall to say that his wife Vincenza, also forty-two, had given birth to a boy the day before, 12 February, in the rented house where they lived. The boy was named Giuseppe, and the parish priest sent word the next day that he had been baptized.[^birth-giuseppe-circelli-1827] Giuseppe and his wife Anna Rita were born two years and about a week apart, in the same small town.

Giuseppe lost both parents young. His father Donato died on 8 November 1839, when Giuseppe was twelve, and his mother Vincenza on 18 October 1843, when he was sixteen.[^death-donato-circelli-1839][^death-vincenza-minichillo-1843]

media.transcription:
ATTI DI MATRIMONIO. Numero 16. [Margin:] Belfiore Lionardantonio / Circelli Maria Donata

L'anno milleottocento ottantaquattro addì ventisette di gennaio a ore anti meridiane nove e minuti cinquantacinque, nella Casa comunale di Sanbartolomeo in Galdo, aperta al pubblico.

Avanti di me Mosa [o Morra?] Giuseppe, Sindaco, Uffiziale dello Stato Civile, vestito in forma ufficiale sono personalmente comparsi:

1. Belfiore Lionardantonio, di anni ventitre, contadino, nato in Sanbartolomeo in Galdo, residente in detto Comune, figlio di padre ignoto, residente in [vuoto], e di madre ignota, residente in [vuoto];

2. Circelli Maria Donata, di anni ventuno, contadina, nata in Sanbartolomeo in Galdo, residente in detto Comune, figlia del fu Giuseppe, residente in vita qui, e della fu Mansolina [lettura incerta] Mita, residente in vita in detto Comune,

i quali mi hanno richiesto di unirli in matrimonio: a questo effetto mi hanno presentato il documento sotto descritto; e dall'esame di questo, nonchè di quelli già prodotti all'atto della richiesta delle pubblicazioni, i quali tutti, muniti del mio visto, inserisco nel volume degli allegati a questo registro, risultandomi nulla ostare alla celebrazione del loro matrimonio, ho letto agli sposi gli articoli centotrenta, centotrentuno e centotrentadue del Codice Civile, e quindi ho domandato allo sposo se intende di prendere in moglie la qui presente Circelli Maria Donata, e a questa se intende di prendere in marito il qui presente Belfiore Lionardantonio, ed avendomi ciascuno risposto affermativamente a piena intelligenza anche dei testimoni sotto indicati, ho pronunziato in nome della legge che i medesimi sono uniti in matrimonio.

A quest'atto sono stati presenti Reino [lettura incerta] Domenico, di anni quarantasei, guardia municipale, e Paradiso Giuseppe, di anni sessantasette, donzello municipale, entrambi residenti in questo Comune.

Il documento presentato è il certificato delle pubblicazioni da me eseguite, la prima il tredici e la seconda il venti del corrente mese di gennaio. Al matrimonio suddetto è stato prestato il consenso dal consiglio di famiglia della sposa, come risulta dall'atto di richiesta delle pubblicazioni.

Letto il presente atto agl'intervenuti, si sono meco sottoscritti i soli testimoni, essendo gli altri analfabeti.

[Firme:] Reino Domenico, testimone. Giuseppe Paradiso, testimonio. Giuseppe Mora [?]
media.translation:
MARRIAGE RECORDS. Number 16. [Margin:] Belfiore Lionardantonio / Circelli Maria Donata

In the year eighteen hundred eighty-four, on the twenty-seventh of January, at nine fifty-five in the morning, in the town hall of San Bartolomeo in Galdo, open to the public.

Before me, Giuseppe Mosa [or Morra?], Mayor and Civil Registrar, dressed in official form, there personally appeared:

1. Lionardantonio Belfiore, aged twenty-three, farm worker (contadino), born in San Bartolomeo in Galdo and living in that town, son of an unknown father and an unknown mother (padre ignoto, madre ignota);

2. Maria Donata Circelli, aged twenty-one, farm worker (contadina), born in San Bartolomeo in Galdo and living in that town, daughter of the late Giuseppe, who lived here in his lifetime, and of the late Mansolina [uncertain reading] Mita, who lived in this town in her lifetime,

who asked me to unite them in marriage. For this purpose they presented the document described below. Having examined it, and those already produced when the banns were requested, all of which I have stamped and placed in the volume of attachments to this register, and finding no impediment to the marriage, I read to the couple articles 130, 131 and 132 of the Civil Code. I then asked the groom whether he wished to take as his wife Maria Donata Circelli, here present, and asked her whether she wished to take as her husband Lionardantonio Belfiore, here present. Each answered yes, in the full hearing of the witnesses named below, and I pronounced them united in marriage in the name of the law.

Present at this act were Domenico Reino [uncertain reading], aged forty-six, municipal guard, and Giuseppe Paradiso, aged sixty-seven, municipal usher, both living in this town.

The document presented is the certificate of the banns I published, the first on the thirteenth and the second on the twentieth of this month of January. Consent to the marriage was given by the bride's family council, as shown in the act requesting the banns.

This act was read to those present. Only the witnesses signed it with me, the others being illiterate.

[Signatures:] Domenico Reino, witness. Giuseppe Paradiso, witness. Giuseppe Mora [?]

people.summary_de: Vater von Maria Donata, der in San Bartolomeo in Galdo lebte und bis Januar 1884 bereits gestorben war. Er ist aus einer einzigen Zeile im Heiratsakt seiner Tochter bekannt.
people.story_de:
Giuseppe Circelli ist aus einer einzigen Zeile bekannt. Als seine Tochter Maria Donata im Januar 1884 heiratete, trug der Beamte sie als Tochter „del fu Giuseppe“ ein, des verstorbenen Giuseppe, der zu seinen Lebzeiten in der Stadt gelebt hatte.[^marriage-1884] Damals war er tot, und seine Frau ebenfalls.

Weil keiner der beiden Elternteile mehr lebte, hält der Akt fest, dass die Zustimmung zur Ehe vom Familienrat der Braut kam, dem consiglio di famiglia, einer Gruppe von Verwandten, die an die Stelle verstorbener Eltern traten.[^marriage-1884]

Mehr sagen die Unterlagen in dieser Sammlung nicht über ihn. Sein Alter, sein Beruf und sein Sterbedatum sind nicht bekannt. Circelli war ein häufiger Familienname in San Bartolomeo in Galdo, und die Zivilstandsregister der Stadt sind auf dem Portal Antenati erhalten, sodass sein Sterbeakt und vielleicht auch seine Heirat dort auffindbar sein sollten.[^research-md]

Nachtrag, November 2026. Giuseppes eigene Geschichte beginnt nun in den ältesten Zivilstandsregistern der Stadt. Er war 23, ein Bauer, als er sich am 17. Januar 1850 Anna Rita Mansolino zur Ehe versprach; der Beamte vermerkte, dass seine Eltern, Donato Circelli und Vincenza, beide gestorben waren.[^marriage-circelli-mansolino-1850] Am 3. Januar 1860 meldete er die Zwillingsstöchter Maria Filomena und Maria Lucia an, und am 25. September 1863, um zehn Uhr morgens, brachte er seine neugeborene Tochter Maria Donata zur Eintragung. Sie wurde noch am selben Tag getauft.[^birth-circelli-twins-1860][^birth-maria-donata-1863]

Nachtrag, November 2026: sein eigener Geburtsakt ist nun gefunden. Am 13. Februar 1827 kam sein Vater, Donato Circelli, ein 42-jähriger Landarbeiter aus der Strada Borgo Nuovo, auf das Rathaus, um anzuzeigen, dass seine Frau Vincenza, ebenfalls 42, am Tag zuvor, dem 12. Februar, in dem gemieteten Haus, in dem sie wohnten, einen Jungen geboren hatte. Der Junge erhielt den Namen Giuseppe, und der Pfarrer ließ am nächsten Tag mitteilen, dass er getauft worden war.[^birth-giuseppe-circelli-1827] Giuseppe und seine Frau Anna Rita kamen im Abstand von zwei Jahren und etwa einer Woche zur Welt, in derselben kleinen Stadt.

Giuseppe verlor beide Eltern jung. Sein Vater Donato starb am 8. November 1839, als Giuseppe zwölf war, und seine Mutter Vincenza am 18. Oktober 1843, als er sechzehn war.[^death-donato-circelli-1839][^death-vincenza-minichillo-1843]

people.summary: The earliest child yet found of Donato Circelli and Vincenza Minichillo, born in San Bartolomeo in Galdo in January 1816, eleven years before his brother Giuseppe.
people.story:
Vincenzo Antonio Circelli was born at home in San Bartolomeo in Galdo on 17 January 1816, at the fifteenth hour. That same afternoon his father, Donato Circelli, a farmer of twenty-six, carried the news to the mayor, and the clerk wrote that the boy was born to Donato's lawful wife, Vincenza Minichello.[^birth-vincenzo-antonio-circelli-1816]

Donato and Vincenza had married at the end of December 1810, so Vincenzo Antonio came five years into the marriage. He was the elder brother of Giuseppe, born in 1827, and of Giovanniangelo, born in 1830.[^birth-giuseppe-circelli-1827][^birth-giovanniangelo-circelli-1830] The other Donato Circelli of the town was only a boy in 1816, so the father here is our Donato.

What became of him is not yet known. His marriage, if he married, would be in the San Bartolomeo registers of the 1830s or 1840s.

people.summary_de: Das früheste bisher gefundene Kind von Donato Circelli und Vincenza Minichillo, geboren im Januar 1816 in San Bartolomeo in Galdo, elf Jahre vor seinem Bruder Giuseppe.
people.story_de:
Vincenzo Antonio Circelli kam am 17. Januar 1816 zu Hause in San Bartolomeo in Galdo zur fünfzehnten Stunde zur Welt. Noch am selben Nachmittag brachte sein Vater, Donato Circelli, ein 26-jähriger Bauer, die Nachricht zum Bürgermeister, und der Beamte schrieb, der Junge sei der rechtmäßigen Ehefrau Donatos geboren, Vincenza Minichello.[^birth-vincenzo-antonio-circelli-1816]

Donato und Vincenza hatten Ende Dezember 1810 geheiratet, sodass Vincenzo Antonio fünf Jahre nach der Hochzeit kam. Er war der ältere Bruder von Giuseppe, geboren 1827, und von Giovanniangelo, geboren 1830.[^birth-giuseppe-circelli-1827][^birth-giovanniangelo-circelli-1830] Der andere Donato Circelli der Stadt war 1816 erst ein Junge, der Vater hier ist also unser Donato.

Was aus ihm wurde, ist noch nicht bekannt. Seine Heirat, falls er geheiratet hat, läge in den Registern von San Bartolomeo aus den 1830er oder 1840er Jahren.

people.summary: Giuseppe Circelli's younger brother, born in San Bartolomeo in Galdo in February 1830. A farmer, he married Maria d'Andrea in 1855.
people.story:
Giovanniangelo Circelli was born at home in San Bartolomeo in Galdo on 27 February 1830, at the fifteenth hour, and was baptised the next day. His father Donato, a farmer of Strada Borgo Nuovo, registered the birth; his mother was Vincenza Minichiello.[^birth-giovanniangelo-circelli-1830] He was the younger brother of Giuseppe Circelli, born three years earlier to the same parents on the same street.[^birth-giuseppe-circelli-1827]

He lost his father in 1839 and his mother in 1843.[^death-donato-circelli-1839][^death-vincenza-minichillo-1843] On 1 November 1855, aged twenty-five and working the land, he married Maria d'Andrea, twenty-one, the daughter of a farmer, Romualdo d'Andrea. The civil promise and the church wedding took place on the same day. The act names him as the son of the late Donato and the late Vincenza, and copies of the death acts of his father, his mother and his grandfather were filed with the papers.[^marriage-1855-giovanniangelo-circelli]

In March 1862 a son, Pasqualantonio, was born to a Giovanni Circelli, son of the late Donato, and his wife Maria d'Andrea, aged twenty-eight. The wife's name and age and the late father all fit Giovanniangelo, so this is very probably his son, written with the short form of his name.[^birth-pasqualantonio-circelli-1862]

Update, November 2026. A daughter, Maria Bartolomea, was born at home on 23 September 1867. Her father registered her the next day as Giovanni Circelli, son of the late Donato, a farmer of thirty-seven, and her mother was his wife Maria D'Andrea.[^birth-maria-bartolomea-circelli-1867] Thirty-seven in 1867 fits a birth in 1830, and the wife's name settles it: this is Giovanniangelo again. On 8 February 1890 Maria Bartolomea, twenty-two, married a young farmer, Michele Circelli, in San Bartolomeo. The act says her father Giovanni and her mother Maria were both living in the town, so Giovanniangelo was still alive at about sixty.[^marriage-circelli-circelli-1890] He also had an elder brother, Vincenzo Antonio, born in 1816.[^birth-vincenzo-antonio-circelli-1816]

people.story_de:
Giovanniangelo Circelli kam am 27. Februar 1830 zu Hause in San Bartolomeo in Galdo zur fünfzehnten Stunde zur Welt und wurde am nächsten Tag getauft. Sein Vater Donato, ein Bauer aus der Strada Borgo Nuovo, meldete die Geburt an; seine Mutter war Vincenza Minichiello.[^birth-giovanniangelo-circelli-1830] Er war der jüngere Bruder von Giuseppe Circelli, der drei Jahre zuvor denselben Eltern in derselben Straße geboren worden war.[^birth-giuseppe-circelli-1827]

Er verlor seinen Vater 1839 und seine Mutter 1843.[^death-donato-circelli-1839][^death-vincenza-minichillo-1843] Am 1. November 1855, 25 Jahre alt und auf dem Land arbeitend, heiratete er Maria d'Andrea, 21, die Tochter eines Bauern, Romualdo d'Andrea. Das zivile Eheversprechen und die kirchliche Trauung fanden am selben Tag statt. Der Akt nennt ihn als Sohn des verstorbenen Donato und der verstorbenen Vincenza, und Abschriften der Sterbeakte seines Vaters, seiner Mutter und seines Großvaters wurden zu den Papieren gelegt.[^marriage-1855-giovanniangelo-circelli]

Im März 1862 wurde einem Giovanni Circelli, Sohn des verstorbenen Donato, und seiner Frau Maria d'Andrea, 28 Jahre alt, ein Sohn geboren, Pasqualantonio. Name und Alter der Frau und der verstorbene Vater passen alle zu Giovanniangelo, es ist also sehr wahrscheinlich sein Sohn, geschrieben mit der Kurzform seines Namens.[^birth-pasqualantonio-circelli-1862]

Nachtrag, November 2026. Eine Tochter, Maria Bartolomea, kam am 23. September 1867 zu Hause zur Welt. Ihr Vater ließ sie am nächsten Tag als Giovanni Circelli eintragen, Sohn des verstorbenen Donato, ein 37-jähriger Bauer, und ihre Mutter war seine Frau Maria D'Andrea.[^birth-maria-bartolomea-circelli-1867] 37 Jahre im Jahr 1867 passen zu einer Geburt 1830, und der Name der Frau entscheidet es: das ist wieder Giovanniangelo. Am 8. Februar 1890 heiratete Maria Bartolomea, 22, in San Bartolomeo einen jungen Bauern, Michele Circelli. Der Akt sagt, ihr Vater Giovanni und ihre Mutter Maria lebten beide in der Stadt, Giovanniangelo war also mit etwa sechzig noch am Leben.[^marriage-circelli-circelli-1890] Er hatte auch einen älteren Bruder, Vincenzo Antonio, geboren 1816.[^birth-vincenzo-antonio-circelli-1816]

people.summary: Maria Donata's mother. Records from 1850, 1860 and 1863 name her Anna Rita (or Rita) Mansolino; earlier research on this site read her name as Marianna Mita.
people.story:
Maria Donata's marriage act of January 1884 names her mother with the word fu, "the late", and records that she too had lived in San Bartolomeo in Galdo.[^marriage-1884]

Her name needs care. Earlier research on this site gave it as Marianna Mita.[^research-md] A close reading of the scan for this profile does not clearly support Marianna: the handwriting looks more like Mansolina or Marsolina, followed by a short surname that reads as Mita. Old Italian civil hands are hard to read, and a second record would settle it. Until then the tree keeps "Marianna Mita" and marks the name as uncertain.[^marriage-1884]

Nothing else is known about her yet: not her age, her parents, or when she died.

Update, November 2026. Three more records have now been found, and they help with her name. When she married Giuseppe Circelli on 17 January 1850 she was Anna Rita Mansolino, twenty-one, the daughter of Francesco Mansolino, a farmer, and of Brigida.[^marriage-circelli-mansolino-1850] Ten years later she was "Rita Manzolino" when her twin girls were born, and "Rita Mansolino" again at Maria Donata's birth in 1863.[^birth-circelli-twins-1860][^birth-maria-donata-1863] That fits the fresh reading of the 1884 act above, which saw "Mansolina" in the handwriting. The tree now shows her as Anna Rita Mansolino and keeps Marianna Mita as the name earlier research gave her.

Update, November 2026: in January 1851 her husband registered their daughter Antonia and named the mother as Margarita Mansolino, twenty-three.[^birth-antonia-circelli-1851] Rita is the usual short form of Margherita, the husband and the age agree, so Margarita, Anna Rita and Rita are the same woman. Antonia is the eldest child of the marriage found so far.

Update, November 2026: her own birth act has now been found. On 20 February 1829 her father, Francesco Mansolino, a farm worker of thirty-five, came to the town hall and declared that his wife Brigida, thirty-eight, had given birth to a daughter that morning. The baby was named Anna Rita, and the parish priest sent word the next day that she had been baptized under that name.[^birth-anna-rita-mansolino-1829] So Anna Rita was her baptismal name, and Rita and Margarita were what the clerks later wrote.

media.alt: The 1884 marriage act of Leonardantonio Belfiore and Maria Donata Circelli from the San Bartolomeo in Galdo civil register, as shown on the Antenati portal
media.transcription:
ATTI DI MATRIMONIO. Numero 16. [Margin:] Belfiore Lionardantonio / Circelli Maria Donata

L'anno milleottocento ottantaquattro addì ventisette di gennaio a ore anti meridiane nove e minuti cinquantacinque, nella Casa comunale di Sanbartolomeo in Galdo, aperta al pubblico.

Avanti di me Mosa [o Morra?] Giuseppe, Sindaco, Uffiziale dello Stato Civile, vestito in forma ufficiale sono personalmente comparsi:

1. Belfiore Lionardantonio, di anni ventitre, contadino, nato in Sanbartolomeo in Galdo, residente in detto Comune, figlio di padre ignoto, residente in [vuoto], e di madre ignota, residente in [vuoto];

2. Circelli Maria Donata, di anni ventuno, contadina, nata in Sanbartolomeo in Galdo, residente in detto Comune, figlia del fu Giuseppe, residente in vita qui, e della fu Mansolina [lettura incerta] Mita, residente in vita in detto Comune,

i quali mi hanno richiesto di unirli in matrimonio: a questo effetto mi hanno presentato il documento sotto descritto; e dall'esame di questo, nonchè di quelli già prodotti all'atto della richiesta delle pubblicazioni, i quali tutti, muniti del mio visto, inserisco nel volume degli allegati a questo registro, risultandomi nulla ostare alla celebrazione del loro matrimonio, ho letto agli sposi gli articoli centotrenta, centotrentuno e centotrentadue del Codice Civile, e quindi ho domandato allo sposo se intende di prendere in moglie la qui presente Circelli Maria Donata, e a questa se intende di prendere in marito il qui presente Belfiore Lionardantonio, ed avendomi ciascuno risposto affermativamente a piena intelligenza anche dei testimoni sotto indicati, ho pronunziato in nome della legge che i medesimi sono uniti in matrimonio.

A quest'atto sono stati presenti Reino [lettura incerta] Domenico, di anni quarantasei, guardia municipale, e Paradiso Giuseppe, di anni sessantasette, donzello municipale, entrambi residenti in questo Comune.

Il documento presentato è il certificato delle pubblicazioni da me eseguite, la prima il tredici e la seconda il venti del corrente mese di gennaio. Al matrimonio suddetto è stato prestato il consenso dal consiglio di famiglia della sposa, come risulta dall'atto di richiesta delle pubblicazioni.

Letto il presente atto agl'intervenuti, si sono meco sottoscritti i soli testimoni, essendo gli altri analfabeti.

[Firme:] Reino Domenico, testimone. Giuseppe Paradiso, testimonio. Giuseppe Mora [?]
media.translation:
MARRIAGE RECORDS. Number 16. [Margin:] Belfiore Lionardantonio / Circelli Maria Donata

In the year eighteen hundred eighty-four, on the twenty-seventh of January, at nine fifty-five in the morning, in the town hall of San Bartolomeo in Galdo, open to the public.

Before me, Giuseppe Mosa [or Morra?], Mayor and Civil Registrar, dressed in official form, there personally appeared:

1. Lionardantonio Belfiore, aged twenty-three, farm worker (contadino), born in San Bartolomeo in Galdo and living in that town, son of an unknown father and an unknown mother (padre ignoto, madre ignota);

2. Maria Donata Circelli, aged twenty-one, farm worker (contadina), born in San Bartolomeo in Galdo and living in that town, daughter of the late Giuseppe, who lived here in his lifetime, and of the late Mansolina [uncertain reading] Mita, who lived in this town in her lifetime,

who asked me to unite them in marriage. For this purpose they presented the document described below. Having examined it, and those already produced when the banns were requested, all of which I have stamped and placed in the volume of attachments to this register, and finding no impediment to the marriage, I read to the couple articles 130, 131 and 132 of the Civil Code. I then asked the groom whether he wished to take as his wife Maria Donata Circelli, here present, and asked her whether she wished to take as her husband Lionardantonio Belfiore, here present. Each answered yes, in the full hearing of the witnesses named below, and I pronounced them united in marriage in the name of the law.

Present at this act were Domenico Reino [uncertain reading], aged forty-six, municipal guard, and Giuseppe Paradiso, aged sixty-seven, municipal usher, both living in this town.

The document presented is the certificate of the banns I published, the first on the thirteenth and the second on the twentieth of this month of January. Consent to the marriage was given by the bride's family council, as shown in the act requesting the banns.

This act was read to those present. Only the witnesses signed it with me, the others being illiterate.

[Signatures:] Domenico Reino, witness. Giuseppe Paradiso, witness. Giuseppe Mora [?]

people.summary_de: Mutter von Maria Donata. Unterlagen von 1850, 1860 und 1863 nennen sie Anna Rita (oder Rita) Mansolino; frühere Recherche auf dieser Website las ihren Namen als Marianna Mita.
people.story_de:
Der Heiratsakt von Maria Donata vom Januar 1884 nennt ihre Mutter mit dem Wort fu, „die Verstorbene“, und hält fest, dass auch sie in San Bartolomeo in Galdo gelebt hatte.[^marriage-1884]

Ihr Name verlangt Sorgfalt. Frühere Recherche auf dieser Website gab ihn als Marianna Mita an.[^research-md] Eine genaue Lesung des Scans für dieses Profil stützt Marianna nicht eindeutig: die Handschrift sieht eher aus wie Mansolina oder Marsolina, gefolgt von einem kurzen Familiennamen, der sich als Mita liest. Alte italienische Zivilstandsschriften sind schwer zu lesen, und eine zweite Unterlage würde die Frage entscheiden. Bis dahin behält der Stammbaum „Marianna Mita“ und kennzeichnet den Namen als unsicher.[^marriage-1884]

Sonst ist über sie noch nichts bekannt: weder ihr Alter noch ihre Eltern oder wann sie starb.

Nachtrag, November 2026. Drei weitere Unterlagen sind nun gefunden, und sie helfen bei ihrem Namen. Als sie am 17. Januar 1850 Giuseppe Circelli heiratete, war sie Anna Rita Mansolino, 21, die Tochter von Francesco Mansolino, einem Bauern, und von Brigida.[^marriage-circelli-mansolino-1850] Zehn Jahre später hieß sie „Rita Manzolino“, als ihre Zwillingstöchter geboren wurden, und bei der Geburt von Maria Donata 1863 wieder „Rita Mansolino“.[^birth-circelli-twins-1860][^birth-maria-donata-1863] Das passt zu der neuen Lesung des Akts von 1884 oben, die in der Handschrift „Mansolina“ sah. Der Stammbaum zeigt sie nun als Anna Rita Mansolino und behält Marianna Mita als den Namen, den die frühere Recherche ihr gab.

Nachtrag, November 2026: im Januar 1851 ließ ihr Mann ihre Tochter Antonia eintragen und nannte die Mutter Margarita Mansolino, 23.[^birth-antonia-circelli-1851] Rita ist die übliche Kurzform von Margherita, Mann und Alter stimmen überein, sodass Margarita, Anna Rita und Rita dieselbe Frau sind. Antonia ist das älteste bisher gefundene Kind der Ehe.

Nachtrag, November 2026: ihr eigener Geburtsakt ist nun gefunden. Am 20. Februar 1829 kam ihr Vater, Francesco Mansolino, ein 35-jähriger Landarbeiter, auf das Rathaus und erklärte, seine Frau Brigida, 38, habe an diesem Morgen eine Tochter geboren. Das Kind erhielt den Namen Anna Rita, und der Pfarrer ließ am nächsten Tag mitteilen, dass sie unter diesem Namen getauft worden war.[^birth-anna-rita-mansolino-1829] Anna Rita war also ihr Taufname, und Rita und Margarita waren das, was die Beamten später schrieben.

people.summary: A foundling who married Maria Donata Circelli in San Bartolomeo in Galdo in 1884. The working identification is that he is Anthony Belfiore, father of nine children in New Rochelle, who died there in 1938.
people.story:
At five minutes to ten on the morning of January 27, 1884, a twenty-three-year-old farm worker stood in the town hall of San Bartolomeo in Galdo to be married. The clerk wrote his name as Belfiore Lionardantonio. In the spaces for his parents he wrote two phrases: padre ignoto, madre ignota. Father unknown, mother unknown.[^marriage-1884]

Those phrases explain the family name. A child of unknown parents had no surname to inherit, so one was given to him. In Italy such children were often left at the ruota degli esposti, the turning wheel set into the wall of a church or hospital, and the institution or the registrar chose their names.[^ctx-ruota] Some foundling surnames marked the child as abandoned, such as Esposito. Others were simply pleasant words, and Belfiore, "beautiful flower", reads like one of these. That is very probably how Leonardantonio came by it, although his own birth and admission records have not been found. It also means the family has no link to the noble Belfiore families of other parts of Italy. The name begins with him.[^research-md]

## The wedding

The marriage act says he was born in San Bartolomeo in Galdo and lived there. His bride was Maria Donata Circelli, twenty-one, also a farm worker, whose parents were both dead. Her consent came from a council of her relatives. The banns had been read on the 13th and the 20th of January. Two town employees stood as witnesses: a municipal guard aged forty-six and the town hall usher, aged sixty-seven. When the act was read back, only the witnesses signed, "the others being illiterate".[^marriage-1884]

## From Leonardantonio to Anthony

No record in this collection uses the name Leonardantonio after 1884. In America the children's father is Anthony or Antonio. The working identification on this site is that he is the same man. It is a strong case but not a proven one, and it rests on several records that point the same way.

- **The name.** Leonardantonio joins Leonardo and Antonio. Using only Antonio, and then Anthony, is an ordinary change for an Italian immigrant.
- **The children's records.** Michael's 1952 death certificate names his parents as Anthony Belfiore and Maria Circelli.[^death-michael-1952] Sammy's obituary calls the nine children's parents "the late Anthony and Maria Cicelli Belfiore".[^standard-star-obit] Indexed records give Frank's and Lena's parents as Antonio Belfiore and Maria D. Circelli.[^frank-index][^lena-index]
- **Citizenship.** In 1918 Michael answered the citizenship question in the column for men who became citizens through their father's naturalization while still minors, writing "Father Papers".[^ww1-michael] His father, then, was in the United States and naturalized before Michael turned twenty-one, around 1906.
- **A return voyage.** Earlier research found a 1909 Ellis Island manifest listing a "Belfiore, Antonio" from San Bartolomeo as a US citizen returning from Italy.[^manifest-1909]
- **A death.** The New York State death index lists an Anthony Belfiore who died in New Rochelle on July 11, 1938, certificate 42184.[^ny-death-index-1938]

Earlier versions of this site argued that Leonardantonio died in Italy before 1896, because Maria Donata crossed that year under her own surname. The records point the other way. Italian women kept their birth surnames in civil and travel records, so a list naming her as Circelli says nothing about her husband. And Frank, born in New Rochelle in November 1897, and Sammy, born there on Christmas Day 1899, both had a father named Anthony or Antonio.[^frank-index][^standard-star-obit]

## What we do not know

When he left San Bartolomeo, and on which ship, is unknown. The transcription of Michael's death certificate gives Michael 58 years of residence in New Rochelle, which would put Michael's arrival around 1894, two years before Maria Donata's crossing.[^death-michael-1952] Whether father and son came first is a fair question, and the 1900 census should answer it, because it asked every immigrant the year they arrived.

His burial place is also unknown. Holy Sepulchre Cemetery in New Rochelle, where Michael was buried, is the first place to ask.

Update, November 2026. He did come to America, and early. Two days before Christmas 1890 a "Leonardo Belfiori" of twenty-nine, from San Bartolomeo, landed in New York on the Hindoustan.[^hindoustan-1890-manifest] In June 1900 the census found him in New Rochelle as Antonio, born in September 1861, married sixteen years, here since 1890 and already a citizen.[^census-1900] Every detail fits the young man who married Maria Donata in 1884.[^marriage-1884] Over the next thirty years the census takers wrote him down as Tony, Anthony and Antonio: a day laborer in 1900, the keeper of a saloon in 1915, a mason in 1925, and by 1920 the owner of the family home.[^census-1905][^census-1915][^census-1920][^census-1925][^census-1930]

Update, November 2026: where the family lived. The census takers wrote down the family's front doors as well as their names. In June 1900 they rented a house at 13 Lawton Street. In 1905 they were at house 62 on a street that looks like Cottage Place. By 1910 Antonio owned 41 Brook Street, with a mortgage, and kept his saloon; the family was still at 41 Brook in 1915 and when Sammy registered for the draft in 1918. In January 1920 the census gives 54 Brook Street, again owned (the numbers on the street may have changed in between). In 1925 they were at 39 Albemarle, and by 1930 Antonio and Marie owned 55 Potter Avenue, a house the census valued at $35,000, with a radio in the parlour.[^census-1900][^census-1905][^census-1910][^census-1915][^ww1-samuel][^census-1920][^census-1925][^census-1930] Brook Street stayed in the family's life: in 1930 their son Michael was renting at 52 Brook Street, a few doors from the old home.[^census-1930-michael]

Update, November 2026: three new pieces. First, his age. He was twenty-three at his wedding in January 1884 and still twenty-three when he registered Michael's birth that December, and twenty-nine when he landed in New York in December 1890. Put together, those ages point to a birth around January 1861.[^marriage-1884][^birth-michele-1884][^hindoustan-1890-manifest] The town's register of births for 1861 is the one year not yet online, which would explain why he has never turned up in the 1860 index.

Second, his name. In March 1882 the midwife of San Bartolomeo reported a baby girl, born dead, "to a woman who does not consent to be named", and the officer wrote that the child was given the name Rosa "and the surname Belfiore".[^birth-rosa-belfiore-1882] It suggests that in this town Belfiore was a surname the civil office gave to children whose parents were not named. Leonardantonio, recorded as son of an unknown father and an unknown mother, very likely received his surname the same way. That is a reasonable reading of the evidence, not yet a proof.

Third, his American paperwork. The Westchester County Archives index lists an Antonio "Belfiora" (once written Zelfiora) who filed a declaration of intention in 1896 and a naturalization petition in 1899, which fits the citizen of the 1900 census and Michael's draft card, where Michael said he was a citizen through his father's papers.[^westchester-naturalization-index][^census-1900][^ww1-michael] The same archives hold a will filed in 1938 for Antonio Belfiore of New Rochelle, the year Anthony Belfiore died there.[^westchester-surrogates-index] Neither document has been seen yet; both are worth a copy request, because a will would name his children.

Update, November 2026. An Anthony Belfiore who died on 11 July 1938 is buried at Holy Sepulchre Cemetery in New Rochelle, the same cemetery as Marie D. Belfiore. The date matches the New Rochelle death in the state index, which makes it more likely still that this is Leonardantonio.[^findagrave-anthony-belfiore][^ny-death-index-1938]

media.caption: Marriage act no. 16, San Bartolomeo in Galdo, January 27, 1884
media.alt: The 1884 marriage act of Leonardantonio Belfiore and Maria Donata Circelli from the San Bartolomeo in Galdo civil register, as shown on the Antenati portal
media.transcription:
ATTI DI MATRIMONIO. Numero 16. [Margin:] Belfiore Lionardantonio / Circelli Maria Donata

L'anno milleottocento ottantaquattro addì ventisette di gennaio a ore anti meridiane nove e minuti cinquantacinque, nella Casa comunale di Sanbartolomeo in Galdo, aperta al pubblico.

Avanti di me Mosa [o Morra?] Giuseppe, Sindaco, Uffiziale dello Stato Civile, vestito in forma ufficiale sono personalmente comparsi:

1. Belfiore Lionardantonio, di anni ventitre, contadino, nato in Sanbartolomeo in Galdo, residente in detto Comune, figlio di padre ignoto, residente in [vuoto], e di madre ignota, residente in [vuoto];

2. Circelli Maria Donata, di anni ventuno, contadina, nata in Sanbartolomeo in Galdo, residente in detto Comune, figlia del fu Giuseppe, residente in vita qui, e della fu Mansolina [lettura incerta] Mita, residente in vita in detto Comune,

i quali mi hanno richiesto di unirli in matrimonio: a questo effetto mi hanno presentato il documento sotto descritto; e dall'esame di questo, nonchè di quelli già prodotti all'atto della richiesta delle pubblicazioni, i quali tutti, muniti del mio visto, inserisco nel volume degli allegati a questo registro, risultandomi nulla ostare alla celebrazione del loro matrimonio, ho letto agli sposi gli articoli centotrenta, centotrentuno e centotrentadue del Codice Civile, e quindi ho domandato allo sposo se intende di prendere in moglie la qui presente Circelli Maria Donata, e a questa se intende di prendere in marito il qui presente Belfiore Lionardantonio, ed avendomi ciascuno risposto affermativamente a piena intelligenza anche dei testimoni sotto indicati, ho pronunziato in nome della legge che i medesimi sono uniti in matrimonio.

A quest'atto sono stati presenti Reino [lettura incerta] Domenico, di anni quarantasei, guardia municipale, e Paradiso Giuseppe, di anni sessantasette, donzello municipale, entrambi residenti in questo Comune.

Il documento presentato è il certificato delle pubblicazioni da me eseguite, la prima il tredici e la seconda il venti del corrente mese di gennaio. Al matrimonio suddetto è stato prestato il consenso dal consiglio di famiglia della sposa, come risulta dall'atto di richiesta delle pubblicazioni.

Letto il presente atto agl'intervenuti, si sono meco sottoscritti i soli testimoni, essendo gli altri analfabeti.

[Firme:] Reino Domenico, testimone. Giuseppe Paradiso, testimonio. Giuseppe Mora [?]
media.translation:
MARRIAGE RECORDS. Number 16. [Margin:] Belfiore Lionardantonio / Circelli Maria Donata

In the year eighteen hundred eighty-four, on the twenty-seventh of January, at nine fifty-five in the morning, in the town hall of San Bartolomeo in Galdo, open to the public.

Before me, Giuseppe Mosa [or Morra?], Mayor and Civil Registrar, dressed in official form, there personally appeared:

1. Lionardantonio Belfiore, aged twenty-three, farm worker (contadino), born in San Bartolomeo in Galdo and living in that town, son of an unknown father and an unknown mother (padre ignoto, madre ignota);

2. Maria Donata Circelli, aged twenty-one, farm worker (contadina), born in San Bartolomeo in Galdo and living in that town, daughter of the late Giuseppe, who lived here in his lifetime, and of the late Mansolina [uncertain reading] Mita, who lived in this town in her lifetime,

who asked me to unite them in marriage. For this purpose they presented the document described below. Having examined it, and those already produced when the banns were requested, all of which I have stamped and placed in the volume of attachments to this register, and finding no impediment to the marriage, I read to the couple articles 130, 131 and 132 of the Civil Code. I then asked the groom whether he wished to take as his wife Maria Donata Circelli, here present, and asked her whether she wished to take as her husband Lionardantonio Belfiore, here present. Each answered yes, in the full hearing of the witnesses named below, and I pronounced them united in marriage in the name of the law.

Present at this act were Domenico Reino [uncertain reading], aged forty-six, municipal guard, and Giuseppe Paradiso, aged sixty-seven, municipal usher, both living in this town.

The document presented is the certificate of the banns I published, the first on the thirteenth and the second on the twentieth of this month of January. Consent to the marriage was given by the bride's family council, as shown in the act requesting the banns.

This act was read to those present. Only the witnesses signed it with me, the others being illiterate.

[Signatures:] Domenico Reino, witness. Giuseppe Paradiso, witness. Giuseppe Mora [?]

people.summary_de: Ein Findelkind, das 1884 in San Bartolomeo in Galdo Maria Donata Circelli heiratete. Die vorläufige Identifizierung lautet, dass er Anthony Belfiore ist, Vater von neun Kindern in New Rochelle, der dort 1938 starb.
people.story_de:
Fünf Minuten vor zehn am Morgen des 27. Januar 1884 stand ein 23-jähriger Landarbeiter im Rathaus von San Bartolomeo in Galdo, um zu heiraten. Der Beamte schrieb seinen Namen als Belfiore Lionardantonio. In die Felder für seine Eltern schrieb er zwei Wendungen: padre ignoto, madre ignota. Vater unbekannt, Mutter unbekannt.[^marriage-1884]

Diese Wendungen erklären den Familiennamen. Ein Kind unbekannter Eltern hatte keinen Familiennamen zu erben, also wurde ihm einer gegeben. In Italien wurden solche Kinder oft an der ruota degli esposti abgelegt, dem Drehrad, das in die Mauer einer Kirche oder eines Krankenhauses eingelassen war, und die Anstalt oder der Standesbeamte wählte ihre Namen.[^ctx-ruota] Manche Findelnamen kennzeichneten das Kind als ausgesetzt, etwa Esposito. Andere waren einfach angenehme Wörter, und Belfiore, „schöne Blume“, liest sich wie eines davon. Sehr wahrscheinlich kam Leonardantonio so zu dem Namen, obwohl seine eigene Geburts- und Aufnahmeunterlage nicht gefunden worden ist. Es bedeutet auch, dass die Familie keine Verbindung zu den adligen Familien Belfiore in anderen Teilen Italiens hat. Der Name beginnt mit ihm.[^research-md]

## Die Hochzeit

Der Heiratsakt sagt, er sei in San Bartolomeo in Galdo geboren und habe dort gelebt. Seine Braut war Maria Donata Circelli, 21, ebenfalls Landarbeiterin, deren Eltern beide tot waren. Ihre Zustimmung kam von einem Rat ihrer Verwandten. Das Aufgebot war am 13. und am 20. Januar verlesen worden. Zwei städtische Bedienstete standen als Zeugen: ein Gemeindewächter von 46 Jahren und der Amtsdiener des Rathauses, 67 Jahre alt. Als der Akt zurückgelesen wurde, unterschrieben nur die Zeugen, „the others being illiterate“ (die übrigen waren des Schreibens unkundig).[^marriage-1884]

## Von Leonardantonio zu Anthony

Keine Unterlage in dieser Sammlung verwendet den Namen Leonardantonio nach 1884. In America heißt der Vater der Kinder Anthony oder Antonio. Die vorläufige Identifizierung auf dieser Website lautet, dass er derselbe Mann ist. Es ist ein starkes Indiz, aber kein bewiesenes, und es ruht auf mehreren Unterlagen, die in dieselbe Richtung weisen.

- **Der Name.** Leonardantonio verbindet Leonardo und Antonio. Nur Antonio zu verwenden und dann Anthony ist eine gewöhnliche Änderung für einen italienischen Einwanderer.
- **Die Unterlagen der Kinder.** Die Sterbeurkunde von Michael von 1952 nennt seine Eltern Anthony Belfiore und Maria Circelli.[^death-michael-1952] Der Nachruf auf Sammy nennt die Eltern der neun Kinder „the late Anthony and Maria Cicelli Belfiore“ (die verstorbenen Anthony und Maria Cicelli Belfiore).[^standard-star-obit] Indexierte Unterlagen geben die Eltern von Frank und Lena als Antonio Belfiore und Maria D. Circelli an.[^frank-index][^lena-index]
- **Staatsbürgerschaft.** 1918 beantwortete Michael die Frage zur Staatsbürgerschaft in der Spalte für Männer, die durch die Einbürgerung ihres Vaters Staatsbürger wurden, solange sie noch minderjährig waren, und schrieb „Father Papers“ (Papiere des Vaters).[^ww1-michael] Sein Vater war also in den United States und vor Michaels 21. Geburtstag eingebürgert, um 1906.
- **Eine Rückreise.** Frühere Recherche fand ein Manifest von Ellis Island von 1909, das einen „Belfiore, Antonio“ aus San Bartolomeo als US-Staatsbürger aufführt, der aus Italien zurückkehrte.[^manifest-1909]
- **Ein Tod.** Der Sterbeindex des Staates New York führt einen Anthony Belfiore, der am 11. Juli 1938 in New Rochelle starb, Urkunde 42184.[^ny-death-index-1938]

Frühere Fassungen dieser Website argumentierten, Leonardantonio sei vor 1896 in Italien gestorben, weil Maria Donata in jenem Jahr unter ihrem eigenen Familiennamen übersetzte. Die Unterlagen weisen in die andere Richtung. Italienische Frauen behielten in Zivilstands- und Reiseunterlagen ihren Geburtsnamen, eine Liste, die sie als Circelli nennt, sagt also nichts über ihren Mann. Und Frank, geboren im November 1897 in New Rochelle, und Sammy, dort am Weihnachtstag 1899 geboren, hatten beide einen Vater namens Anthony oder Antonio.[^frank-index][^standard-star-obit]

## Was wir nicht wissen

Wann er San Bartolomeo verließ und auf welchem Schiff, ist unbekannt. Die Abschrift der Sterbeurkunde von Michael gibt Michael 58 Jahre Aufenthalt in New Rochelle, was Michaels Ankunft um 1894 legen würde, zwei Jahre vor der Überfahrt von Maria Donata.[^death-michael-1952] Ob Vater und Sohn zuerst kamen, ist eine berechtigte Frage, und die Volkszählung von 1900 sollte sie beantworten, denn sie fragte jeden Einwanderer nach dem Jahr der Ankunft.

Auch seine Grabstätte ist unbekannt. Der Holy Sepulchre Cemetery in New Rochelle, wo Michael begraben wurde, ist der erste Ort, an dem man fragen sollte.

Nachtrag, November 2026. Er kam nach America, und früh. Zwei Tage vor Weihnachten 1890 landete ein „Leonardo Belfiori“, 29, aus San Bartolomeo, auf der Hindoustan in New York.[^hindoustan-1890-manifest] Im Juni 1900 fand die Volkszählung ihn in New Rochelle als Antonio, geboren im September 1861, seit sechzehn Jahren verheiratet, seit 1890 hier und bereits Staatsbürger.[^census-1900] Jedes Detail passt zu dem jungen Mann, der 1884 Maria Donata heiratete.[^marriage-1884] Über die nächsten dreißig Jahre schrieben die Zähler ihn als Tony, Anthony und Antonio: 1900 Tagelöhner, 1915 Inhaber eines Saloons, 1925 Maurer, und schon 1920 Eigentümer des Familienhauses.[^census-1905][^census-1915][^census-1920][^census-1925][^census-1930]

Nachtrag, November 2026: wo die Familie wohnte. Die Zähler schrieben die Haustüren der Familie ebenso auf wie ihre Namen. Im Juni 1900 mieteten sie ein Haus in der 13 Lawton Street. 1905 waren sie im Haus 62 einer Straße, die wie Cottage Place aussieht. 1910 besaß Antonio die 41 Brook Street, mit einer Hypothek, und führte seinen Saloon; die Familie war 1915 noch in der 41 Brook und auch, als Sammy sich 1918 zur Musterung eintrug. Im Januar 1920 gibt die Volkszählung die 54 Brook Street an, wieder im Eigentum (die Hausnummern der Straße können sich inzwischen geändert haben). 1925 waren sie in der 39 Albemarle, und 1930 besaßen Antonio und Marie die 55 Potter Avenue, ein Haus, das die Volkszählung auf $35,000 schätzte, mit einem Radio im Wohnzimmer.[^census-1900][^census-1905][^census-1910][^census-1915][^ww1-samuel][^census-1920][^census-1925][^census-1930] Die Brook Street blieb im Leben der Familie: 1930 mietete ihr Sohn Michael in der 52 Brook Street, ein paar Türen vom alten Haus entfernt.[^census-1930-michael]

Nachtrag, November 2026: drei neue Stücke. Erstens sein Alter. Bei seiner Hochzeit im Januar 1884 war er 23 und noch 23, als er im Dezember die Geburt von Michael anmeldete, und 29, als er im Dezember 1890 in New York landete. Zusammengenommen weisen diese Altersangaben auf eine Geburt um Januar 1861.[^marriage-1884][^birth-michele-1884][^hindoustan-1890-manifest] Das Geburtsregister der Stadt für 1861 ist das eine Jahr, das noch nicht online ist, was erklären würde, warum er im Index von 1860 nie aufgetaucht ist.

Zweitens sein Name. Im März 1882 meldete die Hebamme von San Bartolomeo ein tot geborenes Mädchen, „to a woman who does not consent to be named“ (einer Frau, die nicht genannt werden will), und der Beamte schrieb, dem Kind werde der Name Rosa gegeben „and the surname Belfiore“ (und der Familienname Belfiore).[^birth-rosa-belfiore-1882] Das legt nahe, dass Belfiore in dieser Stadt ein Familienname war, den das Zivilstandsamt Kindern gab, deren Eltern nicht genannt wurden. Leonardantonio, eingetragen als Sohn eines unbekannten Vaters und einer unbekannten Mutter, erhielt seinen Familiennamen sehr wahrscheinlich auf dieselbe Weise. Das ist eine vernünftige Lesung der Belege, noch kein Beweis.

Drittens seine amerikanischen Papiere. Der Index der Westchester County Archives führt einen Antonio „Belfiora“ (einmal Zelfiora geschrieben), der 1896 eine Absichtserklärung und 1899 ein Einbürgerungsgesuch einreichte, was zum Staatsbürger der Volkszählung von 1900 und zu Michaels Musterungskarte passt, auf der Michael angab, er sei durch die Papiere seines Vaters Staatsbürger.[^westchester-naturalization-index][^census-1900][^ww1-michael] Dieselben Archive verwahren ein 1938 eingereichtes Testament für Antonio Belfiore aus New Rochelle, dem Jahr, in dem Anthony Belfiore dort starb.[^westchester-surrogates-index] Keines der beiden Dokumente ist bisher gesehen worden; beide sind eine Bitte um eine Kopie wert, denn ein Testament würde seine Kinder nennen.

Nachtrag, November 2026. Ein Anthony Belfiore, der am 11. Juli 1938 starb, ist auf dem Holy Sepulchre Cemetery in New Rochelle begraben, demselben Friedhof wie Marie D. Belfiore. Das Datum passt zum Tod in New Rochelle im Index des Staates, was es noch wahrscheinlicher macht, dass dies Leonardantonio ist.[^findagrave-anthony-belfiore][^ny-death-index-1938]

people.summary: Born in San Bartolomeo in Galdo around 1862, married Leonardantonio Belfiore in 1884, and crossed to New York on the SS Oregon in December 1896. She raised nine children in New Rochelle.
people.story:
Maria Donata Circelli could not write her name. When she married in January 1884 she was twenty-one, a farm worker, and an orphan: the clerk wrote both her parents' names after the word fu, "the late". With her parents dead, the consent for her marriage came from a council of her relatives.[^marriage-1884]

She was born in San Bartolomeo in Galdo, a hill town in the province of Benevento, where Circelli is one of the old family names.[^marriage-1884][^research-md] Her husband was Leonardantonio Belfiore, a foundling two years older. Their son Michele, later Michael, was born on 15 December 1884, eleven months after the wedding.[^birth-michele-1884]

## The crossing

On December 2, 1896, the steamship Oregon reached New York from Genoa and Naples. On its passenger list, at line 413, was "Circelli, Maria Doreta". Earlier research recorded her age as 34, which agrees with the marriage act.[^oregon-1896-index] Doreta is very probably a clerk's version of Donata, and the source of the "Maria D." in later records.

She traveled under her own surname. That was normal for an Italian married woman, whose legal surname did not change at marriage, and it should not be read as a sign that she was a widow. Her arrival came in the last months of the first Ellis Island station, a wooden complex that burned in June 1897. Most passenger manifests from those years were lost in the fire. Lists like hers survive because the Customs Service kept its own copies.[^ctx-ellis-nps][^ctx-ellis-foundation]

Whether Michael crossed with her is not known. The full list page would show any child on the lines after hers. The page shared on this site as the Oregon list does not include her line.[^customs-list-page]

## New Rochelle

By November 1897 the family was in New Rochelle, New York, where Frank was born. Sammy followed on Christmas Day 1899.[^frank-index][^standard-star-obit] In all she raised nine children who survived to be named in Sammy's obituary: Michael, Frank, Joseph and Sammy, and Rose, Caroline, Mollie, Phyl and Mary.[^standard-star-obit] Three of the sons became golf professionals.[^standard-star-obit]

Her Circelli relatives used the same route. In March 1898 Salvatore and Michele Circelli arrived on the Alsatia, giving San Bartolomeo as their home, and in 1911 Salvatore gave New Rochelle as his destination.[^alsatia-1898][^santanna-1911] How they were related to her is not yet known.

## What we do not know

Her date and place of death have not been found. By 1972 Sammy's obituary could call his parents "the late Anthony and Maria".[^standard-star-obit] A New York death certificate under Maria, Mary or Marie Belfiore, or a burial record at Holy Sepulchre Cemetery in New Rochelle, would give the date, and should name her parents, which would help settle her mother's name.

Update, November 2026. Maria Donata's own birth record has been found. On 25 September 1863, at ten in the morning, Giuseppe Circelli, a farmer of thirty-six, carried his new daughter to the town hall of San Bartolomeo in Galdo; her mother was Rita Mansolino. They named her Maria Donata, and she was baptized that same day.[^birth-maria-donata-1863] She had two older sisters, twins born in 1860.[^birth-circelli-twins-1860]

She did not cross the ocean alone. The full page of the Oregon's list shows three children with her: Michele, twelve, and two little girls written as Francesca, nine, and Anna, six.[^oregon-1896-manifest] The New Rochelle censuses show who they were: Filomena, the family's Phyl, and Mary.[^census-1900][^census-1905] By 1900 she was the mother of six living children, and the house went on filling for another eight years.[^census-1900][^census-1915] The state death index records a Marie D. Belfiore who died in New Rochelle on 26 September 1937, the day after her seventy-fourth birthday.[^nysdi-1937]

In 1910 she told the census taker she had borne nine children and that all nine were living, the same nine that the family has always counted.[^census-1910]

Update, November 2026: her homes in New Rochelle. Maria Donata kept house at 13 Lawton Street in 1900, at house 62 in 1905, at 41 Brook Street in 1910 and 1915, at 54 Brook Street in 1920, at 39 Albemarle in 1925 and at 55 Potter Avenue, the family's own house, in 1930.[^census-1900][^census-1905][^census-1910][^census-1915][^census-1920][^census-1925][^census-1930]

Update, November 2026. A Find a Grave memorial for Marie D. Belfiore, born 25 September 1863 and died 26 September 1937, places her grave at Holy Sepulchre Cemetery in New Rochelle, where Michael was later buried.[^findagrave-marie-d-belfiore][^nysdi-1937]

media.caption: Marriage act no. 16, San Bartolomeo in Galdo, January 27, 1884
media.alt: The 1884 marriage act of Leonardantonio Belfiore and Maria Donata Circelli from the San Bartolomeo in Galdo civil register, as shown on the Antenati portal
media.transcription:
ATTI DI MATRIMONIO. Numero 16. [Margin:] Belfiore Lionardantonio / Circelli Maria Donata

L'anno milleottocento ottantaquattro addì ventisette di gennaio a ore anti meridiane nove e minuti cinquantacinque, nella Casa comunale di Sanbartolomeo in Galdo, aperta al pubblico.

Avanti di me Mosa [o Morra?] Giuseppe, Sindaco, Uffiziale dello Stato Civile, vestito in forma ufficiale sono personalmente comparsi:

1. Belfiore Lionardantonio, di anni ventitre, contadino, nato in Sanbartolomeo in Galdo, residente in detto Comune, figlio di padre ignoto, residente in [vuoto], e di madre ignota, residente in [vuoto];

2. Circelli Maria Donata, di anni ventuno, contadina, nata in Sanbartolomeo in Galdo, residente in detto Comune, figlia del fu Giuseppe, residente in vita qui, e della fu Mansolina [lettura incerta] Mita, residente in vita in detto Comune,

i quali mi hanno richiesto di unirli in matrimonio: a questo effetto mi hanno presentato il documento sotto descritto; e dall'esame di questo, nonchè di quelli già prodotti all'atto della richiesta delle pubblicazioni, i quali tutti, muniti del mio visto, inserisco nel volume degli allegati a questo registro, risultandomi nulla ostare alla celebrazione del loro matrimonio, ho letto agli sposi gli articoli centotrenta, centotrentuno e centotrentadue del Codice Civile, e quindi ho domandato allo sposo se intende di prendere in moglie la qui presente Circelli Maria Donata, e a questa se intende di prendere in marito il qui presente Belfiore Lionardantonio, ed avendomi ciascuno risposto affermativamente a piena intelligenza anche dei testimoni sotto indicati, ho pronunziato in nome della legge che i medesimi sono uniti in matrimonio.

A quest'atto sono stati presenti Reino [lettura incerta] Domenico, di anni quarantasei, guardia municipale, e Paradiso Giuseppe, di anni sessantasette, donzello municipale, entrambi residenti in questo Comune.

Il documento presentato è il certificato delle pubblicazioni da me eseguite, la prima il tredici e la seconda il venti del corrente mese di gennaio. Al matrimonio suddetto è stato prestato il consenso dal consiglio di famiglia della sposa, come risulta dall'atto di richiesta delle pubblicazioni.

Letto il presente atto agl'intervenuti, si sono meco sottoscritti i soli testimoni, essendo gli altri analfabeti.

[Firme:] Reino Domenico, testimone. Giuseppe Paradiso, testimonio. Giuseppe Mora [?]
media.translation:
MARRIAGE RECORDS. Number 16. [Margin:] Belfiore Lionardantonio / Circelli Maria Donata

In the year eighteen hundred eighty-four, on the twenty-seventh of January, at nine fifty-five in the morning, in the town hall of San Bartolomeo in Galdo, open to the public.

Before me, Giuseppe Mosa [or Morra?], Mayor and Civil Registrar, dressed in official form, there personally appeared:

1. Lionardantonio Belfiore, aged twenty-three, farm worker (contadino), born in San Bartolomeo in Galdo and living in that town, son of an unknown father and an unknown mother (padre ignoto, madre ignota);

2. Maria Donata Circelli, aged twenty-one, farm worker (contadina), born in San Bartolomeo in Galdo and living in that town, daughter of the late Giuseppe, who lived here in his lifetime, and of the late Mansolina [uncertain reading] Mita, who lived in this town in her lifetime,

who asked me to unite them in marriage. For this purpose they presented the document described below. Having examined it, and those already produced when the banns were requested, all of which I have stamped and placed in the volume of attachments to this register, and finding no impediment to the marriage, I read to the couple articles 130, 131 and 132 of the Civil Code. I then asked the groom whether he wished to take as his wife Maria Donata Circelli, here present, and asked her whether she wished to take as her husband Lionardantonio Belfiore, here present. Each answered yes, in the full hearing of the witnesses named below, and I pronounced them united in marriage in the name of the law.

Present at this act were Domenico Reino [uncertain reading], aged forty-six, municipal guard, and Giuseppe Paradiso, aged sixty-seven, municipal usher, both living in this town.

The document presented is the certificate of the banns I published, the first on the thirteenth and the second on the twentieth of this month of January. Consent to the marriage was given by the bride's family council, as shown in the act requesting the banns.

This act was read to those present. Only the witnesses signed it with me, the others being illiterate.

[Signatures:] Domenico Reino, witness. Giuseppe Paradiso, witness. Giuseppe Mora [?]

people.summary_de: Geboren um 1862 in San Bartolomeo in Galdo, heiratete 1884 Leonardantonio Belfiore und setzte im Dezember 1896 auf der SS Oregon nach New York über. Sie zog neun Kinder in New Rochelle auf.
people.story_de:
Maria Donata Circelli konnte ihren Namen nicht schreiben. Als sie im Januar 1884 heiratete, war sie 21, Landarbeiterin und Waise: der Beamte schrieb die Namen beider Eltern hinter das Wort fu, „die Verstorbene“ bzw. „der Verstorbene“. Da ihre Eltern tot waren, kam die Zustimmung zu ihrer Heirat von einem Rat ihrer Verwandten.[^marriage-1884]

Sie wurde in San Bartolomeo in Galdo geboren, einem Bergstädtchen in der Provinz Benevento, wo Circelli einer der alten Familiennamen ist.[^marriage-1884][^research-md] Ihr Mann war Leonardantonio Belfiore, ein zwei Jahre älteres Findelkind. Ihr Sohn Michele, später Michael, wurde am 15. Dezember 1884 geboren, elf Monate nach der Hochzeit.[^birth-michele-1884]

## Die Überfahrt

Am 2. Dezember 1896 erreichte der Dampfer Oregon New York von Genoa und Naples. Auf seiner Passagierliste, in Zeile 413, stand „Circelli, Maria Doreta“. Frühere Recherche hielt ihr Alter als 34 fest, was mit dem Heiratsakt übereinstimmt.[^oregon-1896-index] Doreta ist sehr wahrscheinlich die Fassung des Beamten von Donata und die Quelle des „Maria D.“ in späteren Unterlagen.

Sie reiste unter ihrem eigenen Familiennamen. Das war für eine verheiratete Italienerin normal, deren gesetzlicher Familienname sich bei der Heirat nicht änderte, und es darf nicht als Zeichen gelesen werden, dass sie Witwe war. Ihre Ankunft fiel in die letzten Monate der ersten Station auf Ellis Island, eines hölzernen Komplexes, der im Juni 1897 abbrannte. Die meisten Passagiermanifeste aus jenen Jahren gingen im Feuer verloren. Listen wie die ihre sind erhalten, weil der Customs Service eigene Abschriften behielt.[^ctx-ellis-nps][^ctx-ellis-foundation]

Ob Michael mit ihr übersetzte, ist nicht bekannt. Die volle Listenseite würde jedes Kind in den Zeilen nach der ihren zeigen. Die Seite, die auf dieser Website als Liste der Oregon geteilt wird, enthält ihre Zeile nicht.[^customs-list-page]

## New Rochelle

Im November 1897 war die Familie in New Rochelle, New York, wo Frank geboren wurde. Sammy folgte am Weihnachtstag 1899.[^frank-index][^standard-star-obit] Insgesamt zog sie neun Kinder auf, die den Nachruf auf Sammy erlebten und darin genannt werden: Michael, Frank, Joseph und Sammy sowie Rose, Caroline, Mollie, Phyl und Mary.[^standard-star-obit] Drei der Söhne wurden Golfprofessionals.[^standard-star-obit]

Ihre Verwandten Circelli nahmen denselben Weg. Im März 1898 kamen Salvatore und Michele Circelli auf der Alsatia an, gaben San Bartolomeo als Heimat an, und 1911 gab Salvatore New Rochelle als Ziel an.[^alsatia-1898][^santanna-1911] Wie sie mit ihr verwandt waren, ist noch nicht bekannt.

## Was wir nicht wissen

Ihr Sterbedatum und der Sterbeort sind nicht gefunden worden. 1972 konnte der Nachruf auf Sammy seine Eltern „the late Anthony and Maria“ (die verstorbenen Anthony und Maria) nennen.[^standard-star-obit] Eine Sterbeurkunde von New York auf den Namen Maria, Mary oder Marie Belfiore oder eine Begräbnisunterlage auf dem Holy Sepulchre Cemetery in New Rochelle würde das Datum geben und sollte ihre Eltern nennen, was helfen würde, den Namen ihrer Mutter zu klären.

Nachtrag, November 2026. Die eigene Geburtsunterlage von Maria Donata ist gefunden worden. Am 25. September 1863, um zehn Uhr morgens, trug Giuseppe Circelli, ein 36-jähriger Bauer, seine neugeborene Tochter zum Rathaus von San Bartolomeo in Galdo; ihre Mutter war Rita Mansolino. Sie nannten sie Maria Donata, und sie wurde noch am selben Tag getauft.[^birth-maria-donata-1863] Sie hatte zwei ältere Schwestern, 1860 geborene Zwillinge.[^birth-circelli-twins-1860]

Sie überquerte den Ozean nicht allein. Die volle Seite der Liste der Oregon zeigt drei Kinder bei ihr: Michele, zwölf, und zwei kleine Mädchen, geschrieben als Francesca, neun, und Anna, sechs.[^oregon-1896-manifest] Die Volkszählungen von New Rochelle zeigen, wer sie waren: Filomena, die Phyl der Familie, und Mary.[^census-1900][^census-1905] 1900 war sie Mutter von sechs lebenden Kindern, und das Haus füllte sich noch weitere acht Jahre.[^census-1900][^census-1915] Der Sterbeindex des Staates verzeichnet eine Marie D. Belfiore, die am 26. September 1937 in New Rochelle starb, am Tag nach ihrem 74. Geburtstag.[^nysdi-1937]

1910 sagte sie dem Zähler, sie habe neun Kinder geboren und alle neun lebten, dieselben neun, die die Familie immer gezählt hat.[^census-1910]

Nachtrag, November 2026: ihre Wohnungen in New Rochelle. Maria Donata führte den Haushalt 1900 in der 13 Lawton Street, 1905 im Haus 62, 1910 und 1915 in der 41 Brook Street, 1920 in der 54 Brook Street, 1925 in der 39 Albemarle und 1930 in der 55 Potter Avenue, dem eigenen Haus der Familie.[^census-1900][^census-1905][^census-1910][^census-1915][^census-1920][^census-1925][^census-1930]

Nachtrag, November 2026. Ein Gedenkeintrag auf Find a Grave für Marie D. Belfiore, geboren am 25. September 1863 und gestorben am 26. September 1937, legt ihr Grab auf den Holy Sepulchre Cemetery in New Rochelle, wo Michael später begraben wurde.[^findagrave-marie-d-belfiore][^nysdi-1937]

people.summary: A man from San Bartolomeo in Galdo who crossed with Michele Circelli in 1898 and was bound for New Rochelle in 1911. Probably a relative of Maria Donata, but the link is unproven.
people.story:
Salvatore Circelli crossed from Naples on the Alsatia, which sailed on February 26, 1898, and reached New York on March 19. He was twenty-eight and could not read or write. On the next line was Michele Circelli, twenty-five. Several men from San Bartolomeo were listed together on that page, and the clerk wrote the town as "S. Bartolomeo in Calore".[^alsatia-1898][^alsatia-1898-index]

Thirteen years later he crossed again. The Sant'Anna left Naples on November 14, 1911, carrying a married Salvatore Circelli, forty-two, whose final destination was New Rochelle, New York.[^santanna-1911] His two ages agree on a birth around 1869, and the second voyage ties a Circelli of San Bartolomeo directly to the town where Maria Donata's family lived.

## How was he related to Maria Donata?

Earlier research called him her brother or cousin. An online index of San Bartolomeo births lists a Salvatore born on January 1, 1869, and a Michele born on March 12, 1871, both sons of Leonardo Circelli and Rosa Pacifico.[^italyheritage-circelli] If those are the two men on the Alsatia, they were not Maria Donata's brothers, because her parents were Giuseppe Circelli and his wife. They could be cousins. The ages do not match perfectly for Michele, and the index has not been checked against the registers, so the relationship stays open.

Update, November 2026: his marriage act has now been read on the original page. On 27 March 1893 Salvatore Circelli, twenty-four, a farm worker born in San Bartolomeo, son of Leonardo and Rosa Pacifico, married Maria Carmela Petrilli, sixteen, daughter of Michele Petrilli. Salvatore signed his own name.[^marriage-circelli-petrilli-1893] That confirms what the online index said about his parents, so he was not Maria Donata's brother. Children named Donato (1894) and Maria Bambina (1897) followed in the town's registers. His wife's name fits the "Maria Circelli" given as his wife on the 1911 crossing, so he is very likely the same Salvatore. Whether Leonardo Circelli was a brother or cousin of Maria Donata's father Giuseppe is still open.

people.summary_de: Ein Mann aus San Bartolomeo in Galdo, der 1898 mit Michele Circelli übersetzte und 1911 nach New Rochelle unterwegs war. Wahrscheinlich ein Verwandter von Maria Donata, die Verbindung ist aber unbewiesen.
people.story_de:
Salvatore Circelli setzte von Naples auf der Alsatia über, die am 26. Februar 1898 auslief und New York am 19. März erreichte. Er war 28 und konnte weder lesen noch schreiben. In der nächsten Zeile stand Michele Circelli, 25. Mehrere Männer aus San Bartolomeo waren auf dieser Seite zusammen aufgeführt, und der Beamte schrieb die Stadt als „S. Bartolomeo in Calore“.[^alsatia-1898][^alsatia-1898-index]

Dreizehn Jahre später setzte er erneut über. Die Sant'Anna verließ Naples am 14. November 1911 mit einem verheirateten Salvatore Circelli, 42, dessen Endziel New Rochelle, New York, war.[^santanna-1911] Seine beiden Altersangaben treffen sich bei einer Geburt um 1869, und die zweite Reise bindet einen Circelli aus San Bartolomeo unmittelbar an die Stadt, in der die Familie von Maria Donata lebte.

## Wie war er mit Maria Donata verwandt?

Frühere Recherche nannte ihn ihren Bruder oder Vetter. Ein Online-Index der Geburten von San Bartolomeo führt einen Salvatore, geboren am 1. Januar 1869, und einen Michele, geboren am 12. März 1871, beide Söhne von Leonardo Circelli und Rosa Pacifico.[^italyheritage-circelli] Wenn das die beiden Männer auf der Alsatia sind, waren sie nicht die Brüder von Maria Donata, denn ihre Eltern waren Giuseppe Circelli und seine Frau. Sie könnten Vettern sein. Die Altersangaben passen bei Michele nicht genau, und der Index ist nicht mit den Registern abgeglichen worden, sodass die Verwandtschaft offen bleibt.

Nachtrag, November 2026: sein Heiratsakt ist nun auf der Originalseite gelesen worden. Am 27. März 1893 heiratete Salvatore Circelli, 24, ein in San Bartolomeo geborener Landarbeiter, Sohn von Leonardo und Rosa Pacifico, Maria Carmela Petrilli, 16, Tochter von Michele Petrilli. Salvatore unterschrieb mit seinem eigenen Namen.[^marriage-circelli-petrilli-1893] Das bestätigt, was der Online-Index über seine Eltern sagte, er war also nicht der Bruder von Maria Donata. In den Registern der Stadt folgten Kinder namens Donato (1894) und Maria Bambina (1897). Der Name seiner Frau passt zu der „Maria Circelli“, die bei der Überfahrt 1911 als seine Frau angegeben ist, er ist also sehr wahrscheinlich derselbe Salvatore. Ob Leonardo Circelli ein Bruder oder ein Vetter von Giuseppe, dem Vater von Maria Donata, war, bleibt offen.

people.story:
Michele Circelli was twenty-five when he reached New York on the Alsatia on March 19, 1898, on the line after Salvatore Circelli. Like Salvatore he could not read or write, and his home was given as San Bartolomeo.[^alsatia-1898][^alsatia-1898-index]

He is sometimes confused with Michael Belfiore, because Michele is the Italian form of Michael. He cannot be the same man. Michael was born in December 1884 and would have been thirteen in 1898, and he was a Belfiore, not a Circelli.[^birth-michele-1884]

An online index of San Bartolomeo births lists a Michele Circelli born on March 12, 1871, son of Leonardo Circelli and Rosa Pacifico.[^italyheritage-circelli] That child would have been twenty-six or twenty-seven in March 1898, close to but not exactly the age on the manifest. If he is the same man, he was probably Maria Donata's cousin rather than her brother. Nothing more is known of him yet.

people.summary: The eldest son and the only one of the four brothers born in Italy. A house painter in New Rochelle for most of his life, married twice, and Seb's great-grandfather.
people.story:
Michael Kirtus Belfiore registered for the draft on September 12, 1918, the day the United States called up every man from 18 to 45.[^ctx-ww1-draft] The registrar described him as of medium height and medium build, with brown eyes and black hair. He was thirty-two, a painter, living at 114 Winyah Avenue in New Rochelle and working for an employer whose name reads as Witmark, at 8 Banks Street.[^ww1-michael]

Two answers on that card matter more than the rest. For citizenship he wrote "Father Papers", in the column for men who became citizens through a father's naturalization before they turned twenty-one. And as his nearest relative he named "(Child) Dorothy Belfiore" of 216 Hamilton Street, Bridgeport, Connecticut.[^ww1-michael] He signed the card himself: Michael, then a word he struck out, then Belfiore, with Kirtus written underneath.

## Born in Italy

He was born on 15 December 1884 at a quarter past ten in the morning, in the family house at no. 17 of a lane whose name reads as Vico Passaro, in San Bartolomeo in Galdo. Two days later his father Leonardantonio, twenty-three, carried him to the town hall to be registered.[^birth-michele-1884] His American papers never quite agreed: the 1918 card and the transcription of his death certificate say 1885, and his 1942 card says 1883.[^ww1-michael][^death-michael-1952][^ww2-michael] The Italian act, written down two days after he was born, settles it.

He was the only one of the four brothers born in Italy.[^standard-star-obit] When he crossed is unknown. His death certificate gives 58 years of residence, which would mean about 1894.[^death-michael-1952] The 1940 census recorded him as naturalized, which matches the 1918 card: he became a citizen through his father.[^census-1940][^ww1-michael]

## Two marriages

Dorothy, the child named on the 1918 card, was living in Bridgeport, apart from her father. Family knowledge holds that she was the daughter of an earlier marriage. The first wife's name is not known.[^family-knowledge]

His second wife was Frances Towey, an Irish-American born in New York in 1897.[^ssdi-frances][^family-knowledge] In April 1940 the census found them at 488 North Avenue, New Rochelle, with their sons Edward, nineteen, and Joseph, seventeen. Michael had left school after seventh grade. He was out of work and had been looking for thirty-six weeks; in 1939 he had worked sixteen weeks as a building painter and earned $200. Frances worked twenty hours a week in a high school cafeteria and had earned $420. Joseph, still in school, worked as a grocery delivery boy.[^census-1940]

## The non-golfing brother

While his three younger brothers became golf professionals at clubs from Daytona Beach to Grosse Pointe, Michael stayed in New Rochelle and painted. Sammy's obituary called him "their non-golfing brother".[^standard-star-obit]

In April 1942 he registered again, in the "old man's registration" for men born between 1877 and 1897.[^ctx-ww2-fourth] He lived at 48 Coligni Avenue and had no telephone. His employer was Alfred A. Last of 141 Chauncey Avenue. The person who would always know his address was "Wife, same address".[^ww2-michael]

He died at New Rochelle Hospital on January 16, 1952, of arteriosclerotic heart disease, and was buried at Holy Sepulchre Cemetery three days later. Frances was the informant on his death certificate. His last address was 46 Mechanic Street.[^death-michael-1952] His grandson William, Seb's uncle, was not yet two.[^family-william]

Update, November 2026. Michael crossed with his mother on the Oregon in December 1896, a boy of twelve listed as Michele.[^oregon-1896-manifest] In Italy, the 1884 birth index for San Bartolomeo lists "Belfiore Michele Antonio, son of Leonardantonio" as act 440, a number beyond the 417 acts of the main register, so the act sits in a supplementary register that is not online.[^index-births-1884] His cards and censuses give 1883 and 1885, so the act itself, once it could be read, would settle his year.

Two more censuses tell us about the years between his marriages. In January 1920 Michael was a widower of thirty-four, lodging with a family in New Rochelle and managing a bowling alley of his own; the same census also lists a "Mike", thirty-six, at his parents' home, very likely the same man counted twice.[^census-1920-michael][^census-1920] By 1930 he was married to Frances, working again as a house painter, with Dorothy, seventeen, and the boys Edward and Joseph at home.[^census-1930-michael] On that census he gave his age at first marriage as thirty-seven, which seems to describe his marriage to Frances about 1920 rather than his first.

Update, November 2026: Michael's addresses. In 1900 and 1905 he lived with his parents on Lawton Street and at house 62. In 1920, a widower, he lodged on North Avenue with John and Margaret Stephens; twenty years later his own family lived at 488 North Avenue. In 1930 he, Frances and the children rented 52 Brook Street, a few doors from 41 and 54 Brook, where his parents had lived.[^census-1900][^census-1905][^census-1920-michael][^census-1930-michael][^census-1940] In 1950 the census found him, aged sixty-five, at home with Frances and Edward.[^census-1950-frances]

Update, November 2026: Michael's birth act has been found and read. It is act 440 of the 1884 births, and it turned out to be online after all, on the 18th page of the register as Antenati now shows it. On 17 December 1884 his father Leonardantonio, twenty-three and a farm worker, came to the town hall to report that his wife Donata Circelli had given birth to a boy at a quarter past ten in the morning of 15 December, at home, at number 17 of a lane whose name reads like Vico Passaro.[^birth-michele-1884] So Michael was born on 15 December 1884, the date his draft cards remembered, in the year that sits between the two years they gave. One of the two witnesses was Antonia Circelli, daughter of the late Giuseppe: his mother's elder sister, his aunt. Nobody in the room but the officer could write.

Update, 27 November 2026. A Fold3 index to the Army's First World War transport lists names Michael K. Belfiore as a passenger on the Princess Matoika, which left Newport News on 20 December 1918. His contact is given as Toney Belfiore of New Rochelle, almost certainly his father Antonio. This is an index line only; the list itself has not been opened, so it is a lead for his wartime service, not a full reading of the record.[^army-transport-princess-matoika-1918]

media.caption: "Sammy Belfore, Last Of 3 Golfing Brothers", The Standard-Star, February 1972
media.alt: Newspaper clipping of Sammy Belfore's 1972 obituary from The Standard-Star, with a photograph of him swinging a club
media.summary: Summary (not a transcription). Headline: "Sammy Belfore, Last Of 3 Golfing Brothers". Reports that Sammy, 72, died in Daytona Beach after a long illness; that he had changed the spelling of his name and had long been pro at the Seabreeze Golf and Tennis Club; that he was born on Christmas Day 1899 in New Rochelle to "the late Anthony and Maria Cicelli Belfiore", one of four brothers and five sisters; that Sammy, Frank and Joseph took up golf professionally when most pros were foreign-born; that Sam started as assistant pro at Wykagyl Country Club and went to Seabreeze in 1948 after 36 years in golf; that Frank ran the golf shop at the Daytona club and Joe was pro at Grosse Pointe, Michigan; that Frank, Joe and "their non-golfing brother, Michael" had died. Survivors: son Sammy Jr. (Daytona Beach), daughter Mrs. Patricia Fleming (Birmingham, Mich.), sisters Rose and Caroline Belfiore (Wykagyl Gardens), Mrs. Anthony (Mollie) Drew (Davenport Avenue, New Rochelle), Mrs. Angelo (Phyl) Paternostro (Hartford, Conn.), Mrs. Joseph (Mary) D'Onofrio (Hollywood, Fla.), and three grandchildren. Photo caption: Sammy as he appeared in 1948 when he became golf pro at Seabreeze.

media.transcription: Num. 440. [Year 1884, 17 December, 10:40 am, before Giuseppe De Paola, assessore delegato.] Appeared Belfiore Leonardantonio, aged 23, contadino, living in Sambartolomeo, who declared that at 10:15 am on the 15th of this month, in the house at Vico Passaro(?) no. 17, a child was born to Circelli [Donata], contadina, his wife. [Name and sex lines damaged; the index reads Michele.] Witnesses: Circelli Antonia fu Giuseppe, 33, contadina, and Popolillo Antonio fu Giovanni, 65, serviente comunale.
