people.summary: Born in New Rochelle on Christmas Day 1899, the first of the three golfing brothers. A Wykagyl shop boy who became a club professional in Duluth and Daytona Beach, taught a blind golfer to play, and later ran the 19th Hole bar on Seabreeze Boulevard.
people.story:
Sammy Belfore stood, by one sports editor's account, "just a fraction over five feet", powerfully built, with a white crest of hair and thick black eyebrows. He wore a silk ascot as a trademark. He would challenge a man to eighteen holes using only a two iron, for a side bet, and win. In his later years he was known to give a useful lesson without getting off his bar stool.[^kahn-1965][^willson-1970] He was born in New Rochelle on Christmas Day 1899, one of the nine children of Anthony and Maria Belfiore.[^standard-star-obit]

## Wykagyl

He started in golf at thirteen, in the golf shop at Wykagyl Country Club in New Rochelle, and was giving lessons by sixteen.[^kahn-1960] He told a reporter years later that he had worked in the shop for "the immortal Alex Smith", and had to wait until the members were off the course before he could sneak in a few holes before dark.[^willson-1970] Smith was a Scottish professional who won the US Open in 1906 and again in 1910, when the New York Times called him the Wykagyl professional.[^ctx-alex-smith]

That background is why the family story matters. Sammy's obituary explained that before the Belfiore brothers, golf professionals and club makers in America were almost all foreign-born, usually Scots. Sam was the first of the three American-born brothers to break through, as assistant professional at Wykagyl.[^standard-star-obit]

## White Sulphur Springs and Florida

He went on to be head professional at White Sulphur Springs, the West Virginia resort now called the Greenbrier. The Daytona papers later reported that he once beat Walter Hagen there by a stroke in a head-to-head match in 1922, and that Sam Snead succeeded him at the resort. Both stories come from Sammy's own recollections as retold in print.[^willson-1966][^kahn-1965][^dben-1972-02-16]

He began spending winters in Daytona Beach in the 1920s. In January 1929 the News-Journal described him as "the diminutive professional at Daytona Highlands", after he shot the best individual round, a 71, at a tournament at Mount Plymouth. His brother Joe was also listed as a Daytona Highlands professional.[^dbnj-1929-01-07] Accounts disagree on when he settled for good: one column says 1924, his news obituary 1938.[^kahn-1960][^dben-1972-02-16]

## Duluth and the blind golfer

In May 1930 his engagement to Virginia Hupp was announced in Detroit by her mother, Mrs. Mae Hupp. The wedding was planned for late June at her mother's home, and the couple were to live in Duluth, Minnesota, in the summer and in Daytona Beach in the winter.[^engagement-1930]

Duluth was his summer job. He was the professional at Ridgeview Country Club there, and it was at Ridgeview that he began teaching Clinton Russell, a Duluth businessman who had been blinded in 1924 when a tire exploded in his face. Between them they worked out a method in which a caddie or friend teed the ball, set his stance for direction and lined up the clubface. In 1931 Russell shot 84 at Ridgeview, and Ripley's Believe It or Not ran the story. On August 20, 1938, Russell beat the English blind golfer W. H. J. Oxenham at Ridgeview, a match that made Time magazine.[^ouse-russell]

Earlier versions of this site put Ridgeview in Westchester and the 1938 match at Wykagyl. The Russell biography in this collection places both in Duluth.

## Daytona Beach

He was head professional at the Daytona Beach Country Club through the 1930s and into the 1940s. On March 13, 1946, he arranged a free exhibition there for Jimmy Demaret, Ben Hogan, Sam Snead and Byron Nelson. Some 4,200 people followed it, and Demaret shot 63. Fourteen years later Sammy could still recount the round shot by shot, and remembered that he had set the pins in difficult places.[^kahn-1960]

In 1947 he oversaw the restoration of the Seabreeze Golf Club for its owner, Earl Warner, and became its pro-manager when it reopened on January 1, 1948, with his brother Frank running the shop. He described the job that February in Golfdom, the golf trade magazine.[^golfdom-1948-02][^golfdom-1948-01][^kahn-1965] The local sports editor later wrote that after dark the clubhouse was a gambling house, and that some of the men who worked for it wore shoulder holsters.[^kahn-1965]

## The 19th Hole

When the club closed, he opened a bar on Seabreeze Boulevard and called it the 19th Hole. The papers give different years for the change, from 1947 to 1951.[^kahn-1960][^kahn-1965][^dben-1972-02-16] A 1951 directory listing put it at 324 Seabreeze Boulevard, as a cocktail lounge, bar and package store.[^research-notes] He held court there for years. The jukebox played "Straight Down the Middle", and one night Rocky Marciano, retired and unbeaten, came in to see him.[^kahn-1965][^dben-1972-02-16] Marciano's mother came from San Bartolomeo in Galdo, the town Sammy's parents had left.[^ctx-marciano] Whether either man knew that is not recorded.

He was a gambler. The same sports editor wrote that he once walked out of a dice game with $27,000 and lost it all the next afternoon on a horse-racing parlay. "I've got nobody to blame but myself," Sammy would say.[^kahn-1965] In March 1965 the sheriff padlocked the bankrupt 19th Hole, and Sammy suffered a severe heart attack the same day.[^kahn-1965][^kahn-1972]

He recovered and lived quietly at 11 South Hollywood Avenue. He died at Halifax Hospital early on Wednesday, February 16, 1972, after a stroke.[^dben-1972-02-16] A requiem Mass was said at Our Lady of Lourdes Church and he was buried at Cedar Hill Memory Gardens.[^dben-1972-02-17]

## Family

His marriage to Virginia Hupp produced a daughter, Patricia Hupp Belfore, born in 1933.[^patricia-findagrave] The marriage ended around 1939, according to earlier research.[^patricia-obit] In November 1948 the Morning Journal announced a fourth birthday party for "Little Sammy Belfore", given by his mother, Mrs. Sammy Belfore, at their home at 217 Jessamine Boulevard. A city directory entry noted in Seb's research lists Sam Belfore at that address with a wife named Louisa.[^dbmj-1948-11-20][^research-notes] His survivors in 1972 were his son Samuel M. Belfore, his daughter Mrs. Patricia Fleming of Birmingham, Michigan, five sisters, and several nieces, including a Mrs. Angelia Carr.[^dben-1972-02-17]

## The name

Sammy is the brother documented as changing the spelling: his New Rochelle obituary says he "had changed the spelling of his name".[^standard-star-obit] Family tradition holds that the shorter Belfore was chosen to fit on golf scorecards. No document in this collection records the reason.[^family-knowledge]

Update, November 2026. Sammy's own World War I draft card, filled in in September 1918 when he was nineteen, describes him as a golf instructor working for Alex Smith at Wykagyl in New Rochelle, the club where the family always said he started.[^ww1-samuel] In February 1942 he registered again in Daytona Beach. That card gives his birthday as 25 December 1898, a year earlier than the family date, and shows him working at the Shenecossett Country Club in New London, Connecticut; the person who would always know his address was Mrs. Virginia H. Belfore of Birmingham, Michigan.[^ww2-samuel] The family's Christmas Day 1899 stays as his birthday here, with 1898 noted beside it.

Update, November 2026: Sammy's addresses. His 1918 card gives 41 Brook Street, New Rochelle, the family home, with his father Tony at the same address. In February 1942 he lived at 1517 South Atlantic Avenue in Daytona Beach and collected his mail at Box 3603, while Virginia stayed at 251 West Maple Avenue in Birmingham, Michigan.[^ww1-samuel][^ww2-samuel] By April 1950 he was the proprietor of a cocktail lounge in Daytona Beach, married to Louisa.[^census-1950-samuel]

Update, 27 November 2026. A family photograph, shared by Sebastian, shows, from left to right, Joe Belfore, Sammy Belfore, Babe Ruth, Lou Gehrig and an unidentified man, who is probably not a Belfore. The date is unknown.[^belfore-brothers-ruth-gehrig-photo]

media.summary: Summary (not a transcription). Headline: "Sammy Belfore, Last Of 3 Golfing Brothers". Reports that Sammy, 72, died in Daytona Beach after a long illness; that he had changed the spelling of his name and had long been pro at the Seabreeze Golf and Tennis Club; that he was born on Christmas Day 1899 in New Rochelle to "the late Anthony and Maria Cicelli Belfiore", one of four brothers and five sisters; that Sammy, Frank and Joseph took up golf professionally when most pros were foreign-born; that Sam started as assistant pro at Wykagyl Country Club and went to Seabreeze in 1948 after 36 years in golf; that Frank ran the golf shop at the Daytona club and Joe was pro at Grosse Pointe, Michigan; that Frank, Joe and "their non-golfing brother, Michael" had died. Survivors: son Sammy Jr. (Daytona Beach), daughter Mrs. Patricia Fleming (Birmingham, Mich.), sisters Rose and Caroline Belfiore (Wykagyl Gardens), Mrs. Anthony (Mollie) Drew (Davenport Avenue, New Rochelle), Mrs. Angelo (Phyl) Paternostro (Hartford, Conn.), Mrs. Joseph (Mary) D'Onofrio (Hollywood, Fla.), and three grandchildren. people.story_de:
Sammy Belfore stand, nach dem Bericht eines Sportredakteurs, „just a fraction over five feet“ (nur ein Bruchteil über fünf Fuß), kräftig gebaut, mit einem weißen Haarschopf und dicken schwarzen Augenbrauen. Er trug ein seidenes Ascot als Markenzeichen. Er forderte einen Mann zu achtzehn Löchern heraus, nur mit einem Eisen 2, um eine Nebenwette, und gewann. In späteren Jahren war er dafür bekannt, eine nützliche Lehrstunde zu geben, ohne von seinem Barhocker aufzustehen.[^kahn-1965][^willson-1970] Er wurde am Weihnachtstag 1899 in New Rochelle geboren, eines der neun Kinder von Anthony und Maria Belfiore.[^standard-star-obit]

## Wykagyl

Er fing mit dreizehn im Golf an, im Golfshop des Wykagyl Country Club in New Rochelle, und gab mit sechzehn schon Unterricht.[^kahn-1960] Jahre später sagte er einem Reporter, er habe im Shop für „the immortal Alex Smith“ (den unsterblichen Alex Smith) gearbeitet und habe warten müssen, bis die Mitglieder vom Platz waren, bevor er sich vor der Dunkelheit ein paar Löcher erschleichen konnte.[^willson-1970] Smith war ein schottischer Professional, der die US Open 1906 und wieder 1910 gewann, als die New York Times ihn den Professional von Wykagyl nannte.[^ctx-alex-smith]

Dieser Hintergrund ist der Grund, warum die Familiengeschichte zählt. Der Nachruf auf Sammy erklärte, dass vor den Brüdern Belfiore die Golfprofessionals und Schlägerbauer in America fast alle im Ausland geboren waren, gewöhnlich Schotten. Sam war der erste der drei in America geborenen Brüder, der durchbrach, als Assistenzprofessional in Wykagyl.[^standard-star-obit]

## White Sulphur Springs und Florida

Er wurde danach leitender Professional in White Sulphur Springs, dem Ferienort in West Virginia, der heute Greenbrier heißt. Die Zeitungen von Daytona berichteten später, er habe dort 1922 Walter Hagen in einem direkten Match um einen Schlag geschlagen, und Sam Snead sei ihm im Ferienort nachgefolgt. Beide Geschichten stammen aus Sammys eigenen Erinnerungen, wie sie im Druck nacherzählt wurden.[^willson-1966][^kahn-1965][^dben-1972-02-16]

Er begann in den 1920er Jahren, die Winter in Daytona Beach zu verbringen. Im Januar 1929 beschrieb ihn das News-Journal als „the diminutive professional at Daytona Highlands“ (den kleinen Professional in Daytona Highlands), nachdem er die beste Einzelrunde gespielt hatte, eine 71, bei einem Turnier in Mount Plymouth. Sein Bruder Joe war ebenfalls als Professional von Daytona Highlands geführt.[^dbnj-1929-01-07] Die Berichte sind sich nicht einig, wann er sich endgültig niederließ: eine Spalte sagt 1924, sein Zeitungsnachruf 1938.[^kahn-1960][^dben-1972-02-16]

## Duluth und der blinde Golfer

Im Mai 1930 wurde seine Verlobung mit Virginia Hupp in Detroit von ihrer Mutter, Mrs. Mae Hupp, bekannt gegeben. Die Hochzeit war für Ende Juni im Haus ihrer Mutter geplant, und das Paar sollte im Sommer in Duluth, Minnesota, und im Winter in Daytona Beach leben.[^engagement-1930]

Duluth war seine Sommerstelle. Er war der Professional im Ridgeview Country Club dort, und in Ridgeview begann er, Clinton Russell zu unterrichten, einen Geschäftsmann aus Duluth, der 1924 erblindet war, als ein Reifen ihm ins Gesicht explodierte. Gemeinsam erarbeiteten sie eine Methode, bei der ein Caddie oder Freund den Ball auftee, seinen Stand für die Richtung setzte und die Schlagfläche ausrichtete. 1931 spielte Russell in Ridgeview eine 84, und Ripley's Believe It or Not brachte die Geschichte. Am 20. August 1938 schlug Russell in Ridgeview den blinden englischen Golfer W. H. J. Oxenham, ein Match, das es in die Zeitschrift Time schaffte.[^ouse-russell]

Frühere Fassungen dieser Website setzten Ridgeview nach Westchester und das Match von 1938 nach Wykagyl. Die Biografie von Russell in dieser Sammlung setzt beides nach Duluth.

## Daytona Beach

Er war die 1930er Jahre hindurch und bis in die 1940er leitender Professional im Daytona Beach Country Club. Am 13. März 1946 richtete er dort eine kostenlose Vorführung für Jimmy Demaret, Ben Hogan, Sam Snead und Byron Nelson aus. Etwa 4.200 Menschen folgten ihr, und Demaret spielte eine 63. Vierzehn Jahre später konnte Sammy die Runde noch Schlag für Schlag nacherzählen und erinnerte sich, dass er die Fahnen an schwierige Stellen gesetzt hatte.[^kahn-1960]

1947 beaufsichtigte er die Wiederherstellung des Seabreeze Golf Club für den Eigentümer Earl Warner und wurde dessen Pro-Manager, als er am 1. Januar 1948 wieder eröffnete, mit seinem Bruder Frank im Shop. Er beschrieb die Stelle in diesem Februar in Golfdom, der Fachzeitschrift für Golf.[^golfdom-1948-02][^golfdom-1948-01][^kahn-1965] Der örtliche Sportredakteur schrieb später, nach Einbruch der Dunkelheit sei das Clubhaus ein Glücksspielhaus gewesen und einige der Männer, die dafür arbeiteten, hätten Schulterhalftern getragen.[^kahn-1965]

## The 19th Hole

Als der Club schloss, eröffnete er eine Bar am Seabreeze Boulevard und nannte sie the 19th Hole. Die Zeitungen geben verschiedene Jahre für den Wechsel an, von 1947 bis 1951.[^kahn-1960][^kahn-1965][^dben-1972-02-16] Ein Verzeichniseintrag von 1951 setzte sie in die 324 Seabreeze Boulevard, als Cocktail-Lounge, Bar und Flaschenladen.[^research-notes] Er hielt dort jahrelang Hof. Die Jukebox spielte „Straight Down the Middle“, und eines Nachts kam Rocky Marciano, zurückgezogen und ungeschlagen, um ihn zu sehen.[^kahn-1965][^dben-1972-02-16] Marcianos Mutter kam aus San Bartolomeo in Galdo, der Stadt, die Sammys Eltern verlassen hatten.[^ctx-marciano] Ob einer der beiden Männer das wusste, ist nicht festgehalten.

Er war ein Spieler. Derselbe Sportredakteur schrieb, er sei einmal mit $27,000 aus einem Würfelspiel gegangen und habe alles am nächsten Nachmittag bei einer Kombinationswette auf Pferderennen verloren. „I've got nobody to blame but myself,“ (Ich habe niemanden zu beschuldigen außer mir selbst,) pflegte Sammy zu sagen.[^kahn-1965] Im März 1965 versiegelte der Sheriff die bankrotte 19th Hole, und Sammy erlitt am selben Tag einen schweren Herzinfarkt.[^kahn-1965][^kahn-1972]

Er erholte sich und lebte still in der 11 South Hollywood Avenue. Er starb am frühen Mittwoch, dem 16. Februar 1972, nach einem Schlaganfall im Halifax Hospital.[^dben-1972-02-16] Eine Totenmesse wurde in der Our Lady of Lourdes Church gelesen, und er wurde auf den Cedar Hill Memory Gardens begraben.[^dben-1972-02-17]

## Familie

Seine Ehe mit Virginia Hupp brachte eine Tochter hervor, Patricia Hupp Belfore, geboren 1933.[^patricia-findagrave] Die Ehe endete um 1939, nach früherer Recherche.[^patricia-obit] Im November 1948 kündigte das Morning Journal eine Feier zum vierten Geburtstag für „Little Sammy Belfore“ an, gegeben von seiner Mutter, Mrs. Sammy Belfore, in ihrem Haus in der 217 Jessamine Boulevard. Ein Stadtverzeichniseintrag, vermerkt in Sebs Recherche, führt Sam Belfore an dieser Adresse mit einer Frau namens Louisa.[^dbmj-1948-11-20][^research-notes] Seine Hinterbliebenen 1972 waren sein Sohn Samuel M. Belfore, seine Tochter Mrs. Patricia Fleming aus Birmingham, Michigan, fünf Schwestern und mehrere Nichten, darunter eine Mrs. Angelia Carr.[^dben-1972-02-17]

## Der Name

Sammy ist der Bruder, für den die Änderung der Schreibweise belegt ist: sein Nachruf in New Rochelle sagt, er „had changed the spelling of his name“ (habe die Schreibweise seines Namens geändert).[^standard-star-obit] Die Familientradition hält fest, das kürzere Belfore sei gewählt worden, damit es auf Golfscorekarten passt. Kein Dokument in dieser Sammlung hält den Grund fest.[^family-knowledge]

Nachtrag, November 2026. Sammys eigene Musterungskarte aus dem Ersten Weltkrieg, ausgefüllt im September 1918, als er neunzehn war, beschreibt ihn als Golflehrer, der für Alex Smith in Wykagyl in New Rochelle arbeitete, dem Club, von dem die Familie immer sagte, er habe dort angefangen.[^ww1-samuel] Im Februar 1942 ließ er sich erneut in Daytona Beach eintragen. Diese Karte gibt seinen Geburtstag als 25. Dezember 1898 an, ein Jahr früher als das Datum der Familie, und zeigt ihn bei der Arbeit im Shenecossett Country Club in New London, Connecticut; die Person, die seine Adresse immer wissen würde, war Mrs. Virginia H. Belfore aus Birmingham, Michigan.[^ww2-samuel] Der Weihnachtstag 1899 der Familie bleibt hier sein Geburtstag, mit 1898 daneben vermerkt.

Nachtrag, November 2026: Sammys Adressen. Seine Karte von 1918 gibt die 41 Brook Street, New Rochelle, an, das Haus der Familie, mit seinem Vater Tony an derselben Adresse. Im Februar 1942 wohnte er in der 1517 South Atlantic Avenue in Daytona Beach und holte seine Post bei Box 3603 ab, während Virginia in der 251 West Maple Avenue in Birmingham, Michigan, blieb.[^ww1-samuel][^ww2-samuel] Im April 1950 war er Inhaber einer Cocktail-Lounge in Daytona Beach, verheiratet mit Louisa.[^census-1950-samuel]

Nachtrag, 27. November 2026. Ein Familienfoto, geteilt von Sebastian, zeigt von links nach rechts Joe Belfore, Sammy Belfore, Babe Ruth, Lou Gehrig und einen nicht identifizierten Mann, der wahrscheinlich kein Belfore ist. Das Datum ist unbekannt.[^belfore-brothers-ruth-gehrig-photo]

people.summary: Sammy's first wife, a 1927 graduate of the State Normal College at Ypsilanti. They married in 1930, and she was the mother of Patricia Hupp Fleming.
people.story:
Virginia Hupp's engagement to Sam Belfore was announced in May 1930 by her mother, Mrs. Mae Hupp. The wedding was set for late June at her mother's home, 251 West Maple Avenue, and the couple planned to spend summers in Duluth, Minnesota, and winters in Daytona Beach.[^engagement-1930]

The announcement says she had attended St. Mary's Academy at Monroe for two years, graduated from Baldwin High School and, in 1927, from the State Normal College at Ypsilanti, and had since done graduate work at the University of Michigan. She had spent a season in Daytona Beach two years earlier. At the engagement party a centerpiece of white sweet peas, shaped like a large golf ball, opened to reveal the couple's cards.[^engagement-1930]

Their daughter, Patricia Hupp Belfore, was born in 1933.[^patricia-findagrave] Earlier research found that the marriage ended around 1939 and that Virginia later married John Moss.[^patricia-obit]

Earlier versions of this site linked her family to the Hupp Motor Car Company of Detroit, maker of the Hupmobile. No document in this collection makes that link, so it is marked as unverified.

Update, November 2026. When Sammy registered for the draft in Daytona Beach in February 1942, the person he named was Mrs. Virginia H. Belfore of 251 West Maple Avenue, Birmingham, Michigan: the same street address that their 1930 engagement notice gave for her mother's home (the notice says Detroit; the draft card shows it was Birmingham, a suburb north of Detroit). The address ties the two records together and suggests Virginia was staying with her mother in Michigan that winter.[^ww2-samuel][^engagement-1930]

people.story_de:
Die Verlobung von Virginia Hupp mit Sam Belfore wurde im Mai 1930 von ihrer Mutter, Mrs. Mae Hupp, bekannt gegeben. Die Hochzeit war für Ende Juni im Haus ihrer Mutter angesetzt, 251 West Maple Avenue, und das Paar plante, die Sommer in Duluth, Minnesota, und die Winter in Daytona Beach zu verbringen.[^engagement-1930]

Die Anzeige sagt, sie habe zwei Jahre die St. Mary's Academy in Monroe besucht, sei von der Baldwin High School und 1927 vom State Normal College in Ypsilanti abgegangen und habe seither ein Aufbaustudium an der University of Michigan betrieben. Sie hatte zwei Jahre zuvor eine Saison in Daytona Beach verbracht. Bei der Verlobungsfeier öffnete sich ein Tischgesteck aus weißen Duftwicken, geformt wie ein großer Golfball, und zeigte die Karten des Paares.[^engagement-1930]

Ihre Tochter, Patricia Hupp Belfore, wurde 1933 geboren.[^patricia-findagrave] Frühere Recherche fand, dass die Ehe um 1939 endete und dass Virginia später John Moss heiratete.[^patricia-obit]

Frühere Fassungen dieser Website verbanden ihre Familie mit der Hupp Motor Car Company of Detroit, Herstellerin des Hupmobile. Kein Dokument in dieser Sammlung stellt diese Verbindung her, sie ist also als unbestätigt gekennzeichnet.

Nachtrag, November 2026. Als Sammy sich im Februar 1942 in Daytona Beach zur Musterung eintragen ließ, nannte er Mrs. Virginia H. Belfore aus der 251 West Maple Avenue, Birmingham, Michigan: dieselbe Straßenadresse, die ihre Verlobungsanzeige von 1930 für das Haus ihrer Mutter angab (die Anzeige sagt Detroit; die Musterungskarte zeigt, dass es Birmingham war, ein Vorort nördlich von Detroit). Die Adresse bindet die beiden Unterlagen zusammen und legt nahe, dass Virginia in diesem Winter bei ihrer Mutter in Michigan blieb.[^ww2-samuel][^engagement-1930]

people.summary: Probably Sammy's second wife and the mother of Sammy Jr. She is known from a 1948 birthday notice and a city directory entry.
people.story:
On November 20, 1948, the Daytona Beach Morning Journal announced a party for "Little Sammy Belfore", four years old that day. It was given by his mother, Mrs. Sammy Belfore, at their home at 217 Jessamine Boulevard, with help from her sister, Mrs. Jack Ollendike.[^dbmj-1948-11-20]

A city directory entry copied into Seb's research notes lists "Sam (Louisa)", golf pro, at the same address.[^research-notes] Together the two records suggest that Sammy's wife in the late 1940s was named Louisa and that she was Sammy Jr.'s mother. Her maiden name, the date of the marriage and the rest of her life are not known. Earlier versions of the tree showed Virginia Hupp as Sammy Jr.'s mother, but his 1944 birth falls after Sammy and Virginia's marriage is reported to have ended.

people.story:
Rose is known from her brother Sammy's obituaries. In February 1972 the Standard-Star listed "the Misses Rose and Caroline Belfiore of Wykagyl Gardens" among his survivors, and the Daytona Beach funeral notice listed "Miss Rose Belfore".[^standard-star-obit][^dben-1972-02-17] She was unmarried and living with her sister Caroline in New Rochelle.

Wykagyl is the New Rochelle neighborhood around the country club where Sammy had started in golf. Her birth year is not documented; earlier versions of the tree showed about 1903 without a source.

Update, November 2026. Rose was born on 3 June 1900 and stayed in New Rochelle all her life; in 1930 she was a stenographer, and in 1950 she and her sister Carolyn kept house together.[^ssdi-numident-family][^census-1930][^census-1950-rose] When her brother Joe registered for the draft in Michigan, it was Rose he named as the person who would always know where he was.[^ww2-joe] She died in March 1994.[^ssdi-numident-family]

Update, November 2026. When her brother Joe registered for the draft in 1942, he named Rose, at the Wykagyl Gardens Apartments in New Rochelle, as the person who would always know where he was. She and Carolyn were still at Wykagyl Gardens in 1972, so Rose made her home there for at least thirty years, in the Wykagyl neighbourhood where Sammy had started in golf at the Wykagyl club.[^ww2-joe][^standard-star-obit] In 1950 she was the head of the household, a secretary, with Carolyn beside her.[^census-1950-rose]

media.summary: Summary (not a transcription). Headline: "Sammy Belfore, Last Of 3 Golfing Brothers". Reports that Sammy, 72, died in Daytona Beach after a long illness; that he had changed the spelling of his name and had long been pro at the Seabreeze Golf and Tennis Club; that he was born on Christmas Day 1899 in New Rochelle to "the late Anthony and Maria Cicelli Belfiore", one of four brothers and five sisters; that Sammy, Frank and Joseph took up golf professionally when most pros were foreign-born; that Sam started as assistant pro at Wykagyl Country Club and went to Seabreeze in 1948 after 36 years in golf; that Frank ran the golf shop at the Daytona club and Joe was pro at Grosse Pointe, Michigan; that Frank, Joe and "their non-golfing brother, Michael" had died. Survivors: son Sammy Jr. (Daytona Beach), daughter Mrs. Patricia Fleming (Birmingham, Mich.), sisters Rose and Caroline Belfiore (Wykagyl Gardens), Mrs. Anthony (Mollie) Drew (Davenport Avenue, New Rochelle), Mrs. Angelo (Phyl) Paternostro (Hartford, Conn.), Mrs. Joseph (Mary) D'Onofrio (Hollywood, Fla.), and three grandchildren. Photo caption: Sammy as he appeared in 1948 when he became golf pro at Seabreeze.

Rose ist aus den Nachrufen auf ihren Bruder Sammy bekannt. Im Februar 1972 führte der Standard-Star „the Misses Rose and Caroline Belfiore of Wykagyl Gardens“ (die Fräulein Rose und Caroline Belfiore aus den Wykagyl Gardens) unter seinen Hinterbliebenen, und die Traueranzeige von Daytona Beach führte „Miss Rose Belfore“.[^standard-star-obit][^dben-1972-02-17] Sie war unverheiratet und lebte bei ihrer Schwester Caroline in New Rochelle.

Nachtrag, November 2026. Rose wurde am 3. Juni 1900 geboren und blieb ihr Leben lang in New Rochelle; 1930 war sie Stenografin, und 1950 führten sie und ihre Schwester Carolyn gemeinsam den Haushalt.[^ssdi-numident-family][^census-1930][^census-1950-rose] Als ihr Bruder Joe sich in Michigan zur Musterung eintragen ließ, nannte er Rose als die Person, die immer wissen würde, wo er war.[^ww2-joe] Sie starb im März 1994.[^ssdi-numident-family]

Nachtrag, November 2026. Als ihr Bruder Joe sich 1942 zur Musterung eintragen ließ, nannte er Rose, in den Wykagyl Gardens Apartments in New Rochelle, als die Person, die immer wissen würde, wo er war. Sie und Carolyn waren 1972 noch in den Wykagyl Gardens, Rose hatte dort also mindestens dreißig Jahre ihr Zuhause, im Viertel Wykagyl, in dem Sammy im Club Wykagyl mit dem Golf angefangen hatte.[^ww2-joe][^standard-star-obit] 1950 war sie Vorstand des Haushalts, Sekretärin, mit Carolyn neben ihr.[^census-1950-rose]

people.story:
Caroline is named in both of her brother Sammy's 1972 obituaries. New Rochelle's Standard-Star called her Miss Caroline Belfiore of Wykagyl Gardens; the Daytona Beach funeral notice called her Miss Carol Belfore.[^standard-star-obit][^dben-1972-02-17] She lived with her sister Rose and had not married.

Earlier versions of this site suggested that the Lena Belfiore of an indexed record might be Caroline under a pet name. Lena is a common Italian short form of names ending in -lina or -lena, including Carolina, so the idea is reasonable, but no record links them.[^lena-index]

Update, November 2026. Carolyn was born on 10 March 1902 and died on 21 May 1989.[^ssdi-numident-family] In 1930 she was a dressmaker living at home, and in 1950 she shared a house with Rose.[^census-1930][^census-1950-rose] The censuses suggest that the little Lena of the early records grew up to be Carolyn: Lena appears in 1905, 1915 and 1920, Carolyn from 1925, and the two never appear together.[^census-1905][^census-1915][^census-1920][^census-1925]

people.summary_de: Eine der fünf Schwestern Belfiore, in New Rochelle Caroline genannt und in Daytona Beach Carol. 1972 war sie unverheiratet und lebte bei ihrer Schwester Rose.
people.story_de:
Caroline wird in beiden Nachrufen auf ihren Bruder Sammy von 1972 genannt. Der Standard-Star von New Rochelle nannte sie Miss Caroline Belfiore aus den Wykagyl Gardens; die Traueranzeige von Daytona Beach nannte sie Miss Carol Belfore.[^standard-star-obit][^dben-1972-02-17] Sie lebte bei ihrer Schwester Rose und hatte nicht geheiratet.

Frühere Fassungen dieser Website vermuteten, die Lena Belfiore einer indexierten Unterlage könnte Caroline unter einem Kosenamen sein. Lena ist eine häufige italienische Kurzform von Namen auf -lina oder -lena, darunter Carolina, die Idee ist also vernünftig, aber keine Unterlage verbindet sie.[^lena-index]

Nachtrag, November 2026. Carolyn wurde am 10. März 1902 geboren und starb am 21. Mai 1989.[^ssdi-numident-family] 1930 war sie Schneiderin und lebte zu Hause, und 1950 teilte sie ein Haus mit Rose.[^census-1930][^census-1950-rose] Die Volkszählungen legen nahe, dass die kleine Lena der frühen Unterlagen zu Carolyn heranwuchs: Lena erscheint 1905, 1915 und 1920, Carolyn ab 1925, und die beiden erscheinen nie zusammen.[^census-1905][^census-1915][^census-1920][^census-1925]

people.summary: One of the five Belfiore sisters. She married Anthony Drew and in 1972 was living on Davenport Avenue, New Rochelle.
people.story:
Mollie appears in her brother Sammy's obituaries as "Mrs. Anthony (Mollie) Drew of Davenport Avenue, New Rochelle" and, in Daytona Beach, as "Mrs. Molly Drew".[^standard-star-obit][^dben-1972-02-17] She married Anthony Drew. Nothing else about her is documented here yet.

Update, November 2026. Mollie was the baby of the family, born about 1908.[^census-1915][^census-1920] Her 1926 high school yearbook gives her full name, Mollie Frances Belfiore, and a line her classmates wrote for her: "Molly, of the raven-black hair and eyes, intends to be a nurse." She belonged to the Spanish Club and the Dramatic Club.[^rochellean-1926] In 1930 she was working as a stenographer.[^census-1930] With Anthony Drew she had a daughter, Patricia, and a son, Charles, called Buddy.[^obit-patricia-hendrie-2019][^ssdi-numident-family]

people.summary: One of the five Belfiore sisters. Her full name was Philomena; she married Angelo Paternostro and lived in Hartford, Connecticut.
people.story:
Earlier versions of this site guessed that Phyl was short for Phyllis or Filomena. The Daytona Beach funeral notice for her brother Sammy settles it: it lists "Mrs. Philomena Paternoster" among his sisters. New Rochelle's Standard-Star gave her as "Mrs. Angelo (Phyl) Paternostro, Hartford, Conn."[^dben-1972-02-17][^standard-star-obit] The two papers spell her married name differently.

She married Angelo Paternostro and in 1972 lived in Hartford. Philomena is also a name that Italian families often shortened to Lena, which makes her a second candidate for the Lena Belfiore of an indexed record.[^lena-index]

Update, November 2026. Phyl was the eldest daughter. Born in San Bartolomeo in September 1887, she was the little "Francesca, nine" who crossed on the Oregon with her mother in December 1896, and the New Rochelle census takers wrote her name as Filomena, Philmenia and even Willmena.[^oregon-1896-manifest][^census-1900][^census-1905][^census-1920] On 20 January 1906 she married Angelo Paternoster in New Rochelle.[^marriage-index-1906]

Phyl's own family can now be traced. By 1910 she and Angelo had settled in Bridgeport, Connecticut, with a daughter, Marianna, and a baby son, Dominick. Ten years later they were in Hartford, where they raised five children: Marian, Dominick, Dorothy, Anthony and Carl. By 1930 they owned their home, and by 1940 Phyl had become an American citizen.[^census-1910-paternostro][^census-1920-paternostro][^census-1930-paternostro][^census-1940-paternostro] Her brother Michael's daughter Dorothy was living in Bridgeport in 1918, and it is possible she was close to her aunt's family there; that is still a lead.

Update, November 2026: Phyl's homes. In 1910 she and Angelo rented at 35 Hallett Street in Bridgeport; in 1920 they lived on Goodman Place in Hartford; and by 1930 they owned 397 Woodland Street, Hartford, where they were still living in 1940.[^census-1910-paternostro][^census-1920-paternostro][^census-1930-paternostro][^census-1940-paternostro]

Phyl died in April 1972. Her obituary in the Hartford Courant of 23 April 1972, as indexed, names her husband Angelo, her children Dominic F., Albert A. and Carl D. Paternostro, Mary Bird and Dorothy Ryalls, and her sisters Mary D'Onofrio, Rose Belfiore, Carolyn Belfiore and Molly Drew. It is the only record found that names the Belfiore sisters together.[^obit-index-filomena-paternostro-1972][^ct-death-index-paternostro]

people.summary_de: Eine der fünf Schwestern Belfiore. Ihr voller Name war Philomena; sie heiratete Angelo Paternostro und lebte in Hartford, Connecticut.
people.story_de:
Frühere Fassungen dieser Website vermuteten, Phyl sei die Kurzform von Phyllis oder Filomena. Die Traueranzeige von Daytona Beach für ihren Bruder Sammy entscheidet es: sie führt „Mrs. Philomena Paternoster“ unter seinen Schwestern. Der Standard-Star von New Rochelle gab sie als „Mrs. Angelo (Phyl) Paternostro, Hartford, Conn.“ an.[^dben-1972-02-17][^standard-star-obit] Die beiden Zeitungen schreiben ihren Ehenamen verschieden.

Sie heiratete Angelo Paternostro und lebte 1972 in Hartford. Philomena ist auch ein Name, den italienische Familien oft zu Lena verkürzten, was sie zu einer zweiten Kandidatin für die Lena Belfiore einer indexierten Unterlage macht.[^lena-index]

Nachtrag, November 2026. Phyl war die älteste Tochter. Geboren im September 1887 in San Bartolomeo, war sie die kleine „Francesca, nine“ (Francesca, neun), die im Dezember 1896 mit ihrer Mutter auf der Oregon übersetzte, und die Zähler von New Rochelle schrieben ihren Namen als Filomena, Philmenia und sogar Willmena.[^oregon-1896-manifest][^census-1900][^census-1905][^census-1920] Am 20. Januar 1906 heiratete sie Angelo Paternoster in New Rochelle.[^marriage-index-1906]

Phyls eigene Familie lässt sich nun verfolgen. 1910 hatten sie und Angelo sich in Bridgeport, Connecticut, niedergelassen, mit einer Tochter, Marianna, und einem kleinen Sohn, Dominick. Zehn Jahre später waren sie in Hartford, wo sie fünf Kinder aufzogen: Marian, Dominick, Dorothy, Anthony und Carl. 1930 besaßen sie ihr Haus, und 1940 war Phyl amerikanische Staatsbürgerin geworden.[^census-1910-paternostro][^census-1920-paternostro][^census-1930-paternostro][^census-1940-paternostro] Die Tochter Dorothy ihres Bruders Michael lebte 1918 in Bridgeport, und es ist möglich, dass sie der Familie ihrer Tante dort nahestand; das ist noch ein Hinweis.

Nachtrag, November 2026: Phyls Wohnungen. 1910 mieteten sie und Angelo in der 35 Hallett Street in Bridgeport; 1920 wohnten sie am Goodman Place in Hartford; und 1930 besaßen sie die 397 Woodland Street, Hartford, wo sie 1940 noch wohnten.[^census-1910-paternostro][^census-1920-paternostro][^census-1930-paternostro][^census-1940-paternostro]

Phyl starb im April 1972. Ihr Nachruf im Hartford Courant vom 23. April 1972, wie indexiert, nennt ihren Mann Angelo, ihre Kinder Dominic F., Albert A. und Carl D. Paternostro, Mary Bird und Dorothy Ryalls, und ihre Schwestern Mary D'Onofrio, Rose Belfiore, Carolyn Belfiore und Molly Drew. Es ist die einzige gefundene Unterlage, die die Schwestern Belfiore zusammen nennt.[^obit-index-filomena-paternostro-1972][^ct-death-index-paternostro]

people.summary: Philomena Belfiore's husband, of Hartford, Connecticut.
people.story:
Angelo Paternostro is known as Philomena's husband from Sammy's 1972 obituary, which lists her as Mrs. Angelo (Phyl) Paternostro of Hartford, Connecticut.[^standard-star-obit]

Angelo came from Italy about 1900. In 1910 he was a railroad foreman in Bridgeport; later, in Hartford, he worked in building construction, first as a hod carrier and then as a foreman, and by 1930 he owned the family home.[^census-1910-paternostro][^census-1920-paternostro][^census-1930-paternostro][^census-1940-paternostro]

Angelo probably died in Hartford on 11 March 1964. A Social Security death record for an Angelo Paternostro born 14 September 1882 ends in March 1964 in Connecticut.[^ct-death-index-paternostro][^numident-paternostro]

people.summary: One of the five Belfiore sisters. She married Joseph D'Onofrio and in 1972 lived in Hollywood, Florida.
people.story:
Mary is listed in her brother Sammy's obituaries as "Mrs. Joseph (Mary) D'Onofrio of Hollywood, Fla." and "Mrs. Mary D'Onofrio".[^standard-star-obit][^dben-1972-02-17] Nothing else about her is documented here yet.

Update, November 2026. Mary was born in San Bartolomeo in October 1889 and crossed on the Oregon at six, listed as Anna.[^census-1900][^oregon-1896-manifest] On 10 December 1911 she married Joseph (Giuseppe) D'Onofrio in New Rochelle.[^marriage-index-1911] The D'Onofrio family remembers that the couple settled in Millburn, New Jersey, and raised six children: Leonard, Angelina, Frank, Donald, Raymond and Dolores.[^donofrio-post-2010] Two of their sons' Social Security records name their mother as Mary Belfore or Belfiore.[^ssdi-numident-family]

The censuses fill in the family's homes. Their two eldest, Leonard and Angelina, were born in New Jersey, which fits the D'Onofrio family's memory of New Jersey; by 1920 the family was in Yonkers, where they stayed through 1940, owning their home by 1930.[^census-1920-donofrio][^census-1930-donofrio][^census-1940-donofrio] The family's memory of Millburn is kept here too: the censuses have not yet found them there, but it may belong to the New Jersey years or to later life.[^donofrio-post-2010] In 1910, just before her marriage, Mary seems to appear at home as "Mattie, daughter, eighteen, born in Italy, came in 1896"; with Michael and Phyl living elsewhere, that makes exactly the nine children her mother reported.[^census-1910]

Update, November 2026: Mary's homes. In 1920 Mary and Joseph rented at 23 Lockwood Avenue, Yonkers; by 1930 they owned 91 Buckingham Road; and in 1940 they rented on Beech Street.[^census-1920-donofrio][^census-1930-donofrio][^census-1940-donofrio]

Update, November 2026: the Westchester County Archives index also lists her wedding, as Maria Belfiore and Giuseppe D'Onofrio, under one certificate number in 1911.[^westchester-marriage-index] And it lists a naturalization petition of 1943 by Mary D'Onofrio, with her maiden name Belfiore beside it.[^westchester-naturalization-index] That is a telling detail. As a child she had most likely become an American through her father's naturalization in 1899, but under the law of 1907 an American woman who married a foreign citizen lost her own citizenship. Joseph did not file his first papers until 1922, so Mary, who had lived in America since the age of six, had to apply in her own name. The petition itself, not yet seen, should give her birth date and place and her arrival in 1896.

media.summary: Summary (not a transcription). Headline: "Sammy Belfore, Last Of 3 Golfing Brothers". Reports that Sammy, 72, died in Daytona Beach after a long illness; that he had changed the spelling of his name and had long been pro at the Seabreeze Golf and Tennis Club; that he was born on Christmas Day 1899 in New Rochelle to "the late Anthony and Maria Cicelli Belfiore", one of four brothers and five sisters; that Sammy, Frank and Joseph took up golf professionally when most pros were foreign-born; that Sam started as assistant pro at Wykagyl Country Club and went to Seabreeze in 1948 after 36 years in golf; that Frank ran the golf shop at the Daytona club and Joe was pro at Grosse Pointe, Michigan; that Frank, Joe and "their non-golfing brother, Michael" had died. Survivors: son Sammy Jr. (Daytona Beach), daughter Mrs. Patricia Fleming (Birmingham, Mich.), sisters Rose and Caroline Belfiore (Wykagyl Gardens), Mrs. Anthony (Mollie) Drew (Davenport Avenue, New Rochelle), Mrs. Angelo (Phyl) Paternostro (Hartford, Conn.), Mrs. Joseph (Mary) D'Onofrio (Hollywood, Fla.), and three grandchildren. people.story_de:
Mary ist in den Nachrufen auf ihren Bruder Sammy als „Mrs. Joseph (Mary) D'Onofrio of Hollywood, Fla.“ und „Mrs. Mary D'Onofrio“ geführt.[^standard-star-obit][^dben-1972-02-17] Sonst ist hier noch nichts über sie belegt.

Nachtrag, November 2026. Mary wurde im Oktober 1889 in San Bartolomeo geboren und setzte mit sechs auf der Oregon über, aufgeführt als Anna.[^census-1900][^oregon-1896-manifest] Am 10. Dezember 1911 heiratete sie Joseph (Giuseppe) D'Onofrio in New Rochelle.[^marriage-index-1911] Die Familie D'Onofrio erinnert sich, dass das Paar sich in Millburn, New Jersey, niederließ und sechs Kinder aufzog: Leonard, Angelina, Frank, Donald, Raymond und Dolores.[^donofrio-post-2010] Die Unterlagen der Social Security von zwei ihrer Söhne nennen ihre Mutter Mary Belfore oder Belfiore.[^ssdi-numident-family]

Die Volkszählungen füllen die Wohnungen der Familie. Ihre beiden Ältesten, Leonard und Angelina, wurden in New Jersey geboren, was zur Erinnerung der Familie D'Onofrio an New Jersey passt; 1920 war die Familie in Yonkers, wo sie bis 1940 blieb, und 1930 besaß sie ihr Haus.[^census-1920-donofrio][^census-1930-donofrio][^census-1940-donofrio] Die Erinnerung der Familie an Millburn wird hier ebenfalls bewahrt: die Volkszählungen haben sie dort noch nicht gefunden, aber sie kann zu den Jahren in New Jersey oder zum späteren Leben gehören.[^donofrio-post-2010] 1910, kurz vor ihrer Heirat, scheint Mary zu Hause als „Mattie, daughter, eighteen, born in Italy, came in 1896“ (Mattie, Tochter, achtzehn, geboren in Italien, kam 1896) zu erscheinen; mit Michael und Phyl, die anderswo lebten, macht das genau die neun Kinder, die ihre Mutter angab.[^census-1910]

Nachtrag, November 2026: Marys Wohnungen. 1920 mieteten Mary und Joseph in der 23 Lockwood Avenue, Yonkers; 1930 besaßen sie die 91 Buckingham Road; und 1940 mieteten sie in der Beech Street.[^census-1920-donofrio][^census-1930-donofrio][^census-1940-donofrio]

Nachtrag, November 2026: der Index der Westchester County Archives führt auch ihre Hochzeit, als Maria Belfiore und Giuseppe D'Onofrio, unter einer Urkundennummer im Jahr 1911.[^westchester-marriage-index] Und er führt ein Einbürgerungsgesuch von 1943 von Mary D'Onofrio, mit ihrem Mädchennamen Belfiore daneben.[^westchester-naturalization-index] Das ist ein aufschlussreiches Detail. Als Kind war sie sehr wahrscheinlich durch die Einbürgerung ihres Vaters 1899 Amerikanerin geworden, aber nach dem Gesetz von 1907 verlor eine amerikanische Frau, die einen ausländischen Staatsbürger heiratete, ihre eigene Staatsbürgerschaft. Joseph reichte seine ersten Papiere erst 1922 ein, sodass Mary, die seit dem sechsten Lebensjahr in America lebte, in ihrem eigenen Namen beantragen musste. Das Gesuch selbst, noch nicht gesehen, sollte ihr Geburtsdatum und den Geburtsort und ihre Ankunft 1896 angeben.

people.story:
An indexed record found in earlier research gives a Lena Belfiore, born about 1901, with parents Antonio Belfiore and Maria D. Circelli.[^lena-index] The Research page describes it as the 1940 census, but that cannot be right as written: the 1940 census does not record parents' names. The record behind the index needs to be identified.

Sammy's 1972 obituaries name nine children and no Lena.[^standard-star-obit][^dben-1972-02-17] So either Lena died before 1972, or she is one of the five sisters under a pet name. Lena is a common Italian short form of names such as Filomena and Carolina, and both Philomena (Phyl) and Caroline were among the sisters. Her link to the family is shown with a dashed line until a record settles it.

Update, November 2026. Lena is very likely Carolyn herself, called Lena as a girl (Lena is a common short form of Carolina). See Caroline's profile. Her card stays here until a record settles it.[^census-1915][^census-1920][^census-1925]

Eine in früherer Recherche gefundene indexierte Unterlage gibt eine Lena Belfiore, geboren etwa 1901, mit den Eltern Antonio Belfiore und Maria D. Circelli.[^lena-index] Die Rechercheseite beschreibt sie als die Volkszählung von 1940, aber das kann so nicht stimmen: die Volkszählung von 1940 hält die Namen der Eltern nicht fest. Die Nachrufe auf Sammy von 1972 nennen neun Kinder und keine Lena.[^standard-star-obit][^dben-1972-02-17] Also starb Lena entweder vor 1972, oder sie ist eine der fünf Schwestern unter einem Kosenamen. Lena ist eine häufige italienische Kurzform von Namen wie Filomena und Carolina, und sowohl Philomena (Phyl) als auch Caroline waren unter den Schwestern. Ihre Verbindung zur Familie ist mit einer gestrichelten Linie gezeigt, bis eine Unterlage es entscheidet.

Nachtrag, November 2026. Lena ist sehr wahrscheinlich Carolyn selbst, als Mädchen Lena genannt (Lena ist eine häufige Kurzform von Carolina). Siehe das Profil von Caroline. Ihre Karte bleibt hier, bis eine Unterlage es entscheidet.[^census-1915][^census-1920][^census-1925]

media.alt: Page 265 of the Country Club of Detroit minutes of October 29, 1963, about Joe Belfore's widow, his assistant and his sons
media.transcription:
COUNTRY CLUB OF DETROIT. MINUTES OF MEETING OF THE BOARD OF GOVERNORS. HELD: OCTOBER 29, 1963.
[Page 265] GOLF, GROUNDS AND GREENS COMMITTEE

Mr. Barr announced the formation of a Committee consisting of Charles G. Chapman, Chairman, A. Fred Kammer, Jr., George Haggarty, Carlton M. Higbie, Jr., and Mrs. Harley G. Higbie, for the purpose of interviewing applicants for the position of Golf Professional left vacant by the death of Joe Belfore. The Committee will report its recommendations to the Board, however, selection of the new Golf Professional is to be made by the Board.

Mr. Higbie presented the letter of appreciation from Mrs. Belfore, and a general discussion was had regarding the handling of the Golf Shop and closing the Club accounts with the Estate of Joe Belfore. After discussion it was unanimously agreed that the Club would pay to Mrs. Belfore the sum of Seven hundred and fifty Dollars ($750.00) as a gift to her and to assist her in the settlement of obligations resulting from the long illness of her husband. On the recommendation of Mr. Higbie it was agreed that the Club would pay the sum of One thousand dollars ($1000.00) to Danny Bianco, Assistant Golf Professional, for services rendered during the past golfing season, and in addition, pay him Four hundred dollars ($400.00) for each of the months of January and February of 1964, and Two hundred dollars ($200.00) for the first half of March. Mr. Higbie stated that the Golf Shop would stay open for the Christmas Season and his recommendation that Mrs. Belfore be permitted to continue the Shop until January 2, 1964, was unanimously approved.

A discussion was had regarding the question whether and to what extent golfing privileges should be extended to David and Joseph F., Jr. (Jeffery) Belfore, sons of Joe Belfore.

On recommendation of Mr. Higbie, it was unanimously agreed that golfing privileges limited to them personally and not to guests or members of their respective families be granted to David and Jeffery Belfore, for a period of two (2) years from and after November 1, 1963. Both men shall have the right to sign chits for themselves and have the use of the Men's Grill and Locker Room.

people.story:
The 1963 Country Club of Detroit minutes name Joe Belfore's sons as "David and Joseph F., Jr. (Jeffery) Belfore", and grant both men two years of golfing privileges.[^ccd-minutes-1963]

Earlier research matched him to a death-index entry for a Joseph F. Belfore Jr., born August 21, 1917, who died in February 1982 in Fair Haven, Vermont.[^vt-jeffery] The match is tentative. A 1917 birth would mean his father was born by about 1897, which fits the family's other dates only if Joe was among the first children born in New Rochelle. The suggestion that his middle initial F. stands for Frank, after his uncle, is a guess with no source.

Update, November 2026. The Vermont record of a man born in 1917 is kept in his file, but it is probably someone else: Golfdom's note of a new baby for the Joe Belfores in 1941 and the 1950 census do not fit a man born in 1917.[^golfdom-1941-04][^census-1950-joe] Whether Jeffery is living is not known, so nothing more about him is added here.

Mr. Higbie presented the letter of appreciation from Mrs. Belfore, and a general discussion was had regarding the handling of the Golf Shop and closing the Club accounts with the Estate of Joe Belfore. After discussion it was unanimously agreed that the Club would pay to Mrs. Belfore the sum of Seven hundred and fifty Dollars ($750.00) as a gift to her and to assist her in the settlement of obligations resulting from the long illness of her husband. On the recommendation of Mr. Higbie it was agreed that the Club would pay the sum of One thousand dollars ($1000.00) to Danny Bianco, Assistant Golf Professional, for services rendered during the past golfing season, and in addition, pay him Four hundred dollars ($400.00) for each of the months of January and February of 1964, and Two hundred dollars ($200.00) for the first half of March. Mr. Higbie stated that the Golf Shop would stay open for the Christmas Season and his recommendation that Mrs. Belfore be permitted to continue the Shop until January 2, 1964, was unanimously approved.

A discussion was had regarding the question whether and to what extent golfing privileges should be extended to David and Joseph F., Jr. (Jeffery) Belfore, sons of Joe Belfore.

On recommendation of Mr. Higbie, it was unanimously agreed that golfing privileges limited to them personally and not to guests or members of their respective families be granted to David and Jeffery Belfore, for a period of two (2) years from and after November 1, 1963. Both men shall have the right to sign chits for themselves and have the use of the Men's Grill and Locker Room.

people.story_de:
Das Protokoll des Country Club of Detroit von 1963 nennt die Söhne von Joe Belfore als „David and Joseph F., Jr. (Jeffery) Belfore“ und gewährt beiden Männern zwei Jahre Golfprivilegien.[^ccd-minutes-1963]

Frühere Recherche ordnete ihn einem Sterbeindexeintrag für einen Joseph F. Belfore Jr. zu, geboren am 21. August 1917, der im Februar 1982 in Fair Haven, Vermont, starb.[^vt-jeffery] Die Zuordnung ist vorläufig. Eine Geburt 1917 würde bedeuten, dass sein Vater etwa 1897 geboren war, was zu den anderen Daten der Familie nur passt, wenn Joe zu den ersten in New Rochelle geborenen Kindern gehörte. Die Vermutung, seine mittlere Initiale F. stehe für Frank, nach seinem Onkel, ist eine Vermutung ohne Quelle.

Nachtrag, November 2026. Die Unterlage aus Vermont über einen 1917 geborenen Mann bleibt in seiner Akte, aber es ist wahrscheinlich jemand anders: die Notiz in Golfdom über ein neues Baby der Joe Belfores 1941 und die Volkszählung von 1950 passen nicht zu einem 1917 geborenen Mann.[^golfdom-1941-04][^census-1950-joe] Ob Jeffery lebt, ist nicht bekannt, hier wird also nichts weiter über ihn hinzugefügt.

people.summary: Sammy and Virginia's daughter, born in 1933. An English and theater teacher who married John Fleming and raised four children. She died in 2022 and is buried in Birmingham, Michigan.
people.story:
Patricia Hupp Belfore was born on June 11, 1933, the daughter of Sammy Belfore and Virginia Hupp. Her middle name came from her mother's family.[^patricia-findagrave]

In 1972 both of her father's obituaries listed her as Mrs. Patricia Fleming of Birmingham, Michigan.[^standard-star-obit][^dben-1972-02-17] Earlier research, based on her own obituary, records that she taught English and theater, that she married John Fleming in 1958, that they divorced in 1990, and that they had four children: Lisa, Chris, John and Geoff. The same obituary carries a family story that she was nearly cast as Bonnie Butler in Gone with the Wind.[^patricia-obit]

She died on January 1, 2022, aged eighty-eight, and is buried at Cedar Hill Cemetery in Birmingham, Michigan.[^patricia-findagrave] Where she died is less clear: this site's golfing page says Birmingham, while earlier versions of the tree placed her in Atlantis, Florida.

Sammy's New Rochelle obituary mentions three grandchildren, while Patricia had four children. One may have been born after 1972, or the count may simply be wrong.[^standard-star-obit]

Her funeral home obituary gives her birth as 6 August 1933 in Duluth, where her father spent his summers, and her death as 7 July 2022 in Atlantis, Florida. It says she was survived by her children Lisa, Chris, John and Geoff, four grandchildren, a son-in-law and a daughter-in-law.[^obit-patricia-fleming-2022-text]

people.story_de:
Patricia Hupp Belfore wurde am 11. Juni 1933 geboren, die Tochter von Sammy Belfore und Virginia Hupp. Ihr zweiter Vorname kam aus der Familie ihrer Mutter.[^patricia-findagrave]

1972 führten beide Nachrufe auf ihren Vater sie als Mrs. Patricia Fleming aus Birmingham, Michigan.[^standard-star-obit][^dben-1972-02-17] Frühere Recherche, gestützt auf ihren eigenen Nachruf, hält fest, dass sie Englisch und Theater unterrichtete, dass sie 1958 John Fleming heiratete, dass sie sich 1990 scheiden ließen und dass sie vier Kinder hatten: Lisa, Chris, John und Geoff. Derselbe Nachruf trägt eine Familiengeschichte, sie sei beinahe als Bonnie Butler in Gone with the Wind besetzt worden.[^patricia-obit]

Sie starb am 1. Januar 2022, im Alter von 88, und ist auf dem Cedar Hill Cemetery in Birmingham, Michigan, begraben.[^patricia-findagrave] Wo sie starb, ist weniger klar: die Golfseite dieser Website sagt Birmingham, während frühere Fassungen des Stammbaums sie nach Atlantis, Florida, setzten.

Der Nachruf auf Sammy in New Rochelle erwähnt drei Enkel, während Patricia vier Kinder hatte. Eines kann nach 1972 geboren sein, oder die Zählung kann einfach falsch sein.[^standard-star-obit]

Der Nachruf des Bestattungsinstituts gibt ihre Geburt als 6. August 1933 in Duluth an, wo ihr Vater die Sommer verbrachte, und ihren Tod als 7. Juli 2022 in Atlantis, Florida. Er sagt, sie sei von ihren Kindern Lisa, Chris, John und Geoff überlebt worden, von vier Enkeln, einem Schwiegersohn und einer Schwiegertochter.[^obit-patricia-fleming-2022-text]

people.story:
On November 20, 1948, "Little Sammy Belfore" turned four. His mother, Mrs. Sammy Belfore, gave him a party at their home at 217 Jessamine Boulevard in Daytona Beach, and ten children were invited.[^dbmj-1948-11-20] That places his birth on November 20, 1944. Earlier versions of this site gave about 1935 and showed Virginia Hupp as his mother. A directory entry for the Jessamine Boulevard house names Sammy's wife as Louisa, which makes her his probable mother.[^research-notes]

When his father died in 1972, he was listed as Samuel M. Belfore of Daytona Beach.[^dben-1972-02-17] Earlier versions of the site called him Samuel Alexander, but no source for that is recorded and the 1972 records give the initial M.

He married Julia Clair. Volusia County property records show their Ormond Beach property passing to her trust in January 2025, which suggests he died in late 2024 or early 2025.[^volusia-2025]

people.story_de:
Am 20. November 1948 wurde „Little Sammy Belfore“ vier. Seine Mutter, Mrs. Sammy Belfore, gab ihm eine Feier in ihrem Haus in der 217 Jessamine Boulevard in Daytona Beach, und zehn Kinder waren eingeladen.[^dbmj-1948-11-20] Das legt seine Geburt auf den 20. November 1944. Frühere Fassungen dieser Website gaben etwa 1935 an und zeigten Virginia Hupp als seine Mutter. Ein Verzeichniseintrag für das Haus am Jessamine Boulevard nennt Sammys Frau Louisa, was sie zu seiner wahrscheinlichen Mutter macht.[^research-notes]

Als sein Vater 1972 starb, wurde er als Samuel M. Belfore aus Daytona Beach geführt.[^dben-1972-02-17] Frühere Fassungen der Website nannten ihn Samuel Alexander, aber dafür ist keine Quelle festgehalten, und die Unterlagen von 1972 geben die Initiale M.

Er heiratete Julia Clair. Grundstücksunterlagen von Volusia County zeigen, dass ihr Grundstück in Ormond Beach im Januar 2025 an ihren Trust überging, was nahelegt, dass er Ende 2024 oder Anfang 2025 starb.[^volusia-2025]

people.summary: Giuseppe Circelli's father, a farm worker in San Bartolomeo in Galdo and the oldest Circelli yet found on this line. He died on 8 November 1839.
people.story:
Donato Circelli is the earliest name yet found on the Circelli side of the family. He was the son of Domenico Circelli and Annamaria Catalano, and he worked the land in San Bartolomeo in Galdo.[^death-donato-circelli-1839]

On 13 February 1827, aged forty-two, he registered the birth of his son Giuseppe, born the day before to his wife Vincenza; the family lived on Strada Borgo Nuovo.[^birth-giuseppe-circelli-1827]

Donato died on 8 November 1839, aged forty-six, still married to Vincenza.[^death-donato-circelli-1839] His own father Domenico, then about eighty, died two months later, on 15 January 1840.[^death-domenico-circelli-1840] Ten years on, a copy of Donato's death act was filed with the papers for Giuseppe's wedding.[^processetti-circelli-mansolino-1850]

A Matteo Circelli, also "son of the late Donato", married in the same town in 1855, but his mother was Lucia Catalano. Because Donato was still married to Vincenza when he died, Matteo is more likely the son of another Donato Circelli; that link is not proven.[^matrimoni-1855-matteo-circelli]

Update, November 2026. A second son has been found. Giovanniangelo Circelli was born on 27 February 1830 to Donato and Vincenza, and Donato, who gave his age as forty, registered the birth himself.[^birth-giovanniangelo-circelli-1830] Giovanniangelo married Maria d'Andrea in 1855.[^marriage-1855-giovanniangelo-circelli] In the same month of 1830 a second Donato Circelli, aged twenty-six, of Strada Palazzo, registered a son Giovanni born to Lucia Catalano. That younger Donato was Matteo Circelli's father, so Matteo belongs to a different Circelli family after all.[^birth-giovanni-circelli-1830][^matrimoni-1852-giovanni-circelli]

people.summary_de: Vater von Giuseppe Circelli, Landarbeiter in San Bartolomeo in Galdo und der älteste Circelli, der auf dieser Linie bisher gefunden wurde. Er starb am 8. November 1839.
people.story_de:
Donato Circelli ist der früheste Name, der auf der Circelli-Seite der Familie bisher gefunden wurde. Er war der Sohn von Domenico Circelli und Annamaria Catalano und bewirtschaftete das Land in San Bartolomeo in Galdo.[^death-donato-circelli-1839]

Am 13. Februar 1827, im Alter von 42 Jahren, meldete er die Geburt seines Sohnes Giuseppe an, der am Tag zuvor von seiner Ehefrau Vincenza geboren worden war; die Familie wohnte in der Strada Borgo Nuovo.[^birth-giuseppe-circelli-1827]

Donato starb am 8. November 1839 im Alter von 46 Jahren, noch mit Vincenza verheiratet.[^death-donato-circelli-1839] Sein eigener Vater Domenico, damals etwa 80, starb zwei Monate später, am 15. Januar 1840.[^death-domenico-circelli-1840] Zehn Jahre später wurde eine Abschrift von Donatos Sterbeakt den Unterlagen für Giuseppes Hochzeit beigefügt.[^processetti-circelli-mansolino-1850]

Ein Matteo Circelli, auch „Sohn des verstorbenen Donato“, heiratete 1855 in derselben Stadt, doch seine Mutter war Lucia Catalano. Weil Donato bei seinem Tod noch mit Vincenza verheiratet war, ist Matteo eher der Sohn eines anderen Donato Circelli; diese Verbindung ist nicht nachgewiesen.[^matrimoni-1855-matteo-circelli]

Aktualisierung, November 2026. Ein zweiter Sohn wurde gefunden. Giovanniangelo Circelli wurde am 27. Februar 1830 Donato und Vincenza geboren, und Donato, der sein Alter mit 40 angab, meldete die Geburt selbst an.[^birth-giovanniangelo-circelli-1830] Giovanniangelo heiratete 1855 Maria d'Andrea.[^marriage-1855-giovanniangelo-circelli] Im selben Monat des Jahres 1830 meldete ein zweiter Donato Circelli, 26 Jahre alt, aus der Strada Palazzo, einen Sohn Giovanni an, der Lucia Catalano geboren wurde. Dieser jüngere Donato war der Vater von Matteo Circelli, sodass Matteo schließlich doch einer anderen Circelli-Familie angehört.[^birth-giovanni-circelli-1830][^matrimoni-1852-giovanni-circelli]

people.summary: Giuseppe Circelli's mother, a spinner, daughter of Leonardo Minichillo and Elisabetta delle Donne. Widowed in 1839, she died on 18 October 1843.
people.story:
Vincenza was Giuseppe Circelli's mother. Her son's 1827 birth act and her own death act write her surname Minichillo; the 1850 marriage act is harder to read and looks like Minichilli.[^birth-giuseppe-circelli-1827][^marriage-circelli-mansolino-1850]

She lost her husband Donato in November 1839.[^death-donato-circelli-1839] She died on 18 October 1843, aged fifty-five, described as a spinner (filatrice) and the daughter of the late Leonardo Minichillo and Elisabetta delle Donne.[^death-vincenza-minichillo-1843] A copy of her death act was later filed with Giuseppe's wedding papers.[^processetti-circelli-mansolino-1850]

A second son, Giovanniangelo, was born to her and Donato on 27 February 1830, when she was said to be forty.[^birth-giovanniangelo-circelli-1830]

people.summary_de: Mutter von Giuseppe Circelli, Spinnerin, Tochter von Leonardo Minichillo und Elisabetta delle Donne. 1839 verwitwet, starb sie am 18. Oktober 1843.
people.story_de:
Vincenza war die Mutter von Giuseppe Circelli. Der Geburtsakt ihres Sohnes von 1827 und ihr eigener Sterbeakt schreiben ihren Nachnamen Minichillo; der Heiratsakt von 1850 ist schwerer zu lesen und sieht aus wie Minichilli.[^birth-giuseppe-circelli-1827][^marriage-circelli-mansolino-1850]

Sie verlor ihren Ehemann Donato im November 1839.[^death-donato-circelli-1839] Sie starb am 18. Oktober 1843 im Alter von 55 Jahren, bezeichnet als Spinnerin (filatrice) und als Tochter des verstorbenen Leonardo Minichillo und der Elisabetta delle Donne.[^death-vincenza-minichillo-1843] Eine Abschrift ihres Sterbeakts wurde später Giuseppes Hochzeitsunterlagen beigefügt.[^processetti-circelli-mansolino-1850]

Ein zweiter Sohn, Giovanniangelo, wurde ihr und Donato am 27. Februar 1830 geboren, als ihr Alter mit 40 angegeben wurde.[^birth-giovanniangelo-circelli-1830]

people.summary: A Circelli of San Bartolomeo, son of a late Donato and Lucia Catalano. He is probably not Giuseppe's half-brother. Married Anna Palumbo in 1855.
people.story:
Matteo Circelli was twenty-one and a farmer when he married Anna Palumbo, eighteen, in San Bartolomeo on 7 January 1855. The act calls him the son of the late Donato and of Lucia Catalano, who was still living.[^matrimoni-1855-matteo-circelli] Their daughter Lucia was born a year later.[^nati-1856-circelli]

Giuseppe Circelli's father was also called Donato, so the two men were once thought to be half-brothers. The death records now argue against it. Giuseppe's father Donato died on 8 November 1839, still married to Giuseppe's mother Vincenza, who outlived him until 1843.[^death-donato-circelli-1839][^death-vincenza-minichillo-1843] Matteo was born about 1833, while that marriage was still going, to a different mother. So Matteo's father was most likely another Donato Circelli of the same town, and he is no longer linked to Giuseppe's family in the tree. Circelli was a common name in San Bartolomeo, and the two families may still have been cousins.

Update, November 2026. Matteo's own family has come into view. In February 1830 a Donato Circelli, twenty-six, living on Strada Palazzo, registered the birth of a son Giovanni to his wife Lucia Catalano, twenty-one.[^birth-giovanni-circelli-1830] In February 1852 that Giovanni, now twenty-one, married Concetta Buccione, and the act names him as the son of the late Donato and of Lucia Catalano, the same parents Matteo gave three years later.[^matrimoni-1852-giovanni-circelli] So Matteo had an older brother Giovanni, and their father was a younger Donato, born about 1804. Giuseppe's father, of Strada Borgo Nuovo, was forty-two in 1827 and had his own son Giovanniangelo in the same month of 1830.[^birth-giuseppe-circelli-1827][^birth-giovanniangelo-circelli-1830] Two Donato Circellis, each with a son called Giovanni born in February 1830, explain why the records were so easy to mix up.

people.summary_de: Ein Circelli aus San Bartolomeo, Sohn eines verstorbenen Donato und der Lucia Catalano. Er ist wahrscheinlich nicht Giuseppes Halbbruder. Heiratete 1855 Anna Palumbo.
people.story_de:
Matteo Circelli war 21 Jahre alt und Bauer, als er am 7. Januar 1855 in San Bartolomeo Anna Palumbo, 18, heiratete. Der Akt nennt ihn den Sohn des verstorbenen Donato und der Lucia Catalano, die noch lebte.[^matrimoni-1855-matteo-circelli] Ihre Tochter Lucia wurde ein Jahr später geboren.[^nati-1856-circelli]

Auch der Vater von Giuseppe Circelli hieß Donato, sodass die beiden Männer einmal für Halbbrüder gehalten wurden. Die Sterbeakten sprechen nun dagegen. Giuseppes Vater Donato starb am 8. November 1839, noch verheiratet mit Giuseppes Mutter Vincenza, die ihn bis 1843 überlebte.[^death-donato-circelli-1839][^death-vincenza-minichillo-1843] Matteo wurde etwa 1833 geboren, während diese Ehe noch bestand, von einer anderen Mutter. Matteos Vater war also höchstwahrscheinlich ein anderer Donato Circelli derselben Stadt, und er ist im Stammbaum nicht mehr mit Giuseppes Familie verknüpft. Circelli war in San Bartolomeo ein häufiger Name, und die beiden Familien könnten dennoch Cousins gewesen sein.

Aktualisierung, November 2026. Matteos eigene Familie ist in den Blick gekommen. Im Februar 1830 meldete ein Donato Circelli, 26, wohnhaft in der Strada Palazzo, die Geburt eines Sohnes Giovanni bei seiner Ehefrau Lucia Catalano, 21, an.[^birth-giovanni-circelli-1830] Im Februar 1852 heiratete dieser Giovanni, nun 21, Concetta Buccione, und der Akt nennt ihn als Sohn des verstorbenen Donato und der Lucia Catalano, derselben Eltern, die Matteo drei Jahre später angab.[^matrimoni-1852-giovanni-circelli] Matteo hatte also einen älteren Bruder Giovanni, und ihr Vater war ein jüngerer Donato, geboren etwa 1804. Giuseppes Vater, aus der Strada Borgo Nuovo, war 1827 42 Jahre alt und bekam im selben Monat des Jahres 1830 seinen eigenen Sohn Giovanniangelo.[^birth-giuseppe-circelli-1827][^birth-giovanniangelo-circelli-1830] Zwei Donato Circelli, jeder mit einem Sohn namens Giovanni, der im Februar 1830 geboren wurde, erklären, warum die Akten so leicht zu verwechseln waren.

people.summary: The eldest known child of Giuseppe Circelli and Anna Rita Mansolino, born in January 1851. In 1884 she stood witness at the birth of her nephew Michael.
people.story:
On 18 January 1851 Giuseppe Circelli, a farm worker of twenty-four whose father Donato had died, came before the mayor of San Bartolomeo with a baby girl born to his wife Margarita Mansolino, twenty-three. They lived on strada Borgo. The girl was named Antonia.[^birth-antonia-circelli-1851] She was twelve years older than her sister Maria Donata.

She appears once more, as a grown woman. When her nephew Michael was registered on 17 December 1884, the first witness was "Circelli Antonia fu Giuseppe", thirty-three, a farm worker: the right name, the right father, already dead by then, and the right age.[^birth-michele-1884] Choosing her suggests the Circelli family stayed close to Maria Donata after she married Leonardantonio. Whom Antonia married, and whether she stayed in Italy, is not yet known. The town had several women named Antonia Circelli. The marriages of 1886 and 1890 that carry the name turned out to be weddings of their children, not hers.[^marriages-sbg-1886-1890-circelli]

people.summary_de: Das älteste bekannte Kind von Giuseppe Circelli und Anna Rita Mansolino, geboren im Januar 1851. 1884 trat sie bei der Geburt ihres Neffen Michael als Zeugin auf.
people.story_de:
Am 18. Januar 1851 erschien Giuseppe Circelli, ein 24-jähriger Landarbeiter, dessen Vater Donato gestorben war, vor dem Bürgermeister von San Bartolomeo mit einem neugeborenen Mädchen, das seiner Ehefrau Margarita Mansolino, 23, geboren worden war. Sie wohnten in der strada Borgo. Das Mädchen erhielt den Namen Antonia.[^birth-antonia-circelli-1851] Sie war zwölf Jahre älter als ihre Schwester Maria Donata.

Sie erscheint noch einmal, als erwachsene Frau. Als ihr Neffe Michael am 17. Dezember 1884 eingetragen wurde, war die erste Zeugin „Circelli Antonia fu Giuseppe“ (Tochter des verstorbenen Giuseppe), 33, Landarbeiterin: der richtige Name, der richtige Vater, damals bereits tot, und das richtige Alter.[^birth-michele-1884] Dass man sie wählte, lässt darauf schließen, dass die Familie Circelli auch nach Maria Donatas Heirat mit Leonardantonio eng mit ihr verbunden blieb. Wen Antonia heiratete und ob sie in Italien blieb, ist noch nicht bekannt. In der Stadt gab es mehrere Frauen namens Antonia Circelli. Die Heiraten von 1886 und 1890, die den Namen tragen, erwiesen sich als Hochzeiten von deren Kindern, nicht als ihre.[^marriages-sbg-1886-1890-circelli]

people.summary: One of twin girls born to Giuseppe Circelli and Anna Rita Mansolino on 3 January 1860: an older sister of Maria Donata.
people.story: On 3 January 1860 Giuseppe Circelli, a farmer of thirty, registered the births of twin daughters in San Bartolomeo. Their mother was Rita Mansolino. One twin was named Maria Filomena.[^birth-circelli-twins-1860] She was Maria Donata's sister, three years older. The name Filomena came back a generation later, when Maria Donata named her own eldest daughter Filomena, the Phyl of the family.

people.summary: Born 1856 in San Bartolomeo, son of Vincenzo. Possibly the "Circolo Michele" who sailed beside Leonardantonio in 1890.
people.story: A Michele Circelli was born in San Bartolomeo on 7 January 1856, son of Vincenzo Circelli and Carolina (surname hard to read).[^nati-1856-circelli] Thirty-four years later, on the Hindoustan that brought Leonardo Belfiore to New York in December 1890, the line just above his reads "Circolo Michele", aged thirty-five.[^hindoustan-1890-manifest] The two may be the same man, a townsman of the Circelli family travelling with Maria Donata's husband. He is not Maria Donata's brother, and any closer tie is still a lead.

Er ist nicht Maria Donatas Bruder, und jede engere Verbindung bleibt eine Spur.

people.summary: Remembered in the D'Onofrio family's account of Antonio and Donata Maria's children. She may be one of the known sisters under another name.
people.story: A 2010 account written by Gerard D'Onofrio, from the D'Onofrio side of the family, lists a Carmella among the children of Antonio and Donata Maria Belfiore.[^donofrio-post-2010] The censuses from 1900 to 1930 show nine children and no Carmella, so she may be one of the sisters remembered under another name, perhaps Phyl, whose given name changed more than once in the records.[^census-1900][^census-1905][^census-1920] Her card is kept, as family tradition, until a record settles it.

openQuestions.question: Was she the Carmella Belfiore who died in 1929?
openQuestions.record: A Carmella Belfiore died at Niagara Falls on 25 October 1929 (New York State death index, certificate 63917) and is buried at Holy Sepulchre Cemetery, New Rochelle (Find a Grave memorial 324110471). The death certificate would give her age and parents. A lead only.
openQuestions.question_de: War sie die Carmella Belfiore, die 1929 starb?
openQuestions.record_de: Eine Carmella Belfiore starb am 25. Oktober 1929 in Niagara Falls (Sterbeindex von New York State, Urkunde 63917) und ist auf dem Holy Sepulchre Cemetery, New Rochelle, beigesetzt (Find a Grave Memorial 324110471). Die Sterbeurkunde würde ihr Alter und ihre Eltern nennen. Nur eine Spur.

people.summary: The youngest child of Mary and Joseph D'Onofrio (1934 to 2021). She grew up in Millburn, New Jersey, and raised six children.
people.story:
Dolores is the youngest of Mary and Joseph D'Onofrio's six children.[^donofrio-post-2010][^census-1940-donofrio] She was born in White Plains, New York, on 25 September 1934, and her obituary names her as the daughter of the late Joseph and Mary (nee Belfiore) D'Onofrio.[^obit-dolores-saggio-2021]

She settled in Millburn, New Jersey, the town where her father had worked at his brother Frank's nursery, and graduated from Millburn High School in 1952. She was a homemaker and later worked for the Millburn Township Police Department. She loved feeding her large family, and Sunday gravy dinners brought everyone together; when they were all gathered she would say, "Look at what I made!" She was a movie buff and a sports fan.[^obit-dolores-saggio-2021]

She raised six children, and she left nineteen grandchildren and four great-grandchildren when she died on 15 November 2021. Her brother Raymond's 2002 obituary lists her as his sister, Deloris Saggio.[^obit-dolores-saggio-2021][^obit-index-raymond-donofrio-2002]
people.summary_de: Das jüngste Kind von Mary und Joseph D'Onofrio (1934 bis 2021). Sie wuchs in Millburn, New Jersey, auf und zog sechs Kinder groß.
people.story_de:
Dolores ist die Jüngste der sechs Kinder von Mary und Joseph D'Onofrio.[^donofrio-post-2010][^census-1940-donofrio] Sie wurde am 25. September 1934 in White Plains, New York, geboren, und ihr Nachruf nennt sie als Tochter des verstorbenen Joseph und der Mary (geborene Belfiore) D'Onofrio.[^obit-dolores-saggio-2021]

Sie ließ sich in Millburn, New Jersey, nieder, der Stadt, in der ihr Vater in der Gärtnerei seines Bruders Frank gearbeitet hatte, und machte 1952 ihren Abschluss an der Millburn High School. Sie war Hausfrau und arbeitete später für das Millburn Township Police Department. Sie liebte es, ihre große Familie zu bekochen, und die Sonntagsessen mit Gravy brachten alle zusammen; wenn alle versammelt waren, sagte sie: „Look at what I made!“ (Seht nur, was ich gemacht habe!). Sie war eine leidenschaftliche Filmfanin und Sportfanin.[^obit-dolores-saggio-2021]

Sie zog sechs Kinder groß und hinterließ neunzehn Enkel und vier Urenkel, als sie am 15. November 2021 starb. Der Nachruf ihres Bruders Raymond von 2002 führt sie als seine Schwester Deloris Saggio auf.[^obit-dolores-saggio-2021][^obit-index-raymond-donofrio-2002]

people.story: Joe was born in Port Chester in 1940 to Joseph Anton and Dorothy (Belfiore) Racine, and named Joseph Francis Michael, the last name probably for his grandfather Michael Belfiore. He grew up in Yonkers, studied electrical engineering at Manhattan College, served in the Air Force from 1962 to 1965 at Wright-Patterson, and married Cecelia Nobrega on 1 August 1964. He worked at Bendix as an aerospace engineer for 35 years and died on 16 November 2024, aged 84.[^obit-joseph-racine-2024][^obit-index-dorothy-racine-2004]

Er wuchs in Yonkers auf, studierte Elektrotechnik am Manhattan College, diente von 1962 bis 1965 bei der Air Force in Wright-Patterson und heiratete Cecelia Nobrega am 1. August 1964. Er arbeitete 35 Jahre bei Bendix als Luft- und Raumfahrtingenieur und starb am 16. November 2024 im Alter von 84 Jahren.[^obit-joseph-racine-2024][^obit-index-dorothy-racine-2004]

people.summary: He and Annie Hussey raised Dorothy. The censuses list her as their granddaughter, so he is probably Seb's great-great-grandfather, not her father.
people.story:
Family story, and the census, say that Patrick and his second wife Annie raised Dorothy, Seb's grandmother, after Dorothy's mother died young. The 1930 and 1940 censuses list Dorothy as their granddaughter. They also give her parents' birthplaces as New York. Patrick himself was born in Ireland, so he is not her father on those records. Later obituaries of Annie's children name Dorothy as a sister; that family language is kept beside the census, not in place of it.[^family-knowledge][^hennessy-census-1930-image][^hennessy-census-1940-image][^obit-patricia-dillon-2021][^obit-francis-hennessy-2013][^obit-anne-latino-2024]

Update, November 2026. Patrick was very probably the child baptised on 12 April 1874 at Conahy, County Kilkenny, son of Patrick Hennessy and Kate Brennan. Those are the parents named when he married Anna Marie Hussey on 17 June 1914.[^hennessy-baptism-1874][^hennessy-marriage-1914]

He arrived in New York on 11 January 1894. He declared his intention on 15 September 1905 and was naturalized on 18 October 1905. No passenger list for that January day has been found.[^hennessy-naturalization-1905]

His first wife was Mary, surname not yet known. She is with him in 1905, and by 1910 he was a widower at Premium Point. Their sons were Joseph, Thomas, Henry, and John, called Jack.[^hennessy-census-1905][^hennessy-census-1910][^hennessy-census-1915]

In 1910 his work was with the horses at Premium Point. In 1920 he owned 101 Huguenot Street, a chauffeur for a private family, and he told the census taker that his native tongue was Irish. In 1925 he lived at number 260, in the house of his employer Sidney Williams. In 1930 he and Annie were at 3 Fair Oaks, Premium Point, and in 1940 they were still on Premium Point.[^hennessy-census-1910][^hennessy-census-1920][^hennessy-census-1925][^hennessy-census-1930][^hennessy-census-1940]

A draft card for a Patrick Joseph Hennessy of Huguenot Street gives a birthday of 18 April 1877. That date does not fit the baptism, so the card has been kept as another reading, not as his birthday. A New York State death index entry for Patrick J. Hennessy, died 27 June 1947 at New Rochelle, aged 70, certificate 38983, is probably his. Aged 70 that June fits a birth in 1876 or 1877, which agrees with the draft card and not with the 1874 baptism. Both dates are kept until the death certificate, or another record, settles the year.[^hennessy-wwi-draft][^nys-death-index-1947-hennessy]

Update, 27 November 2026. The 1918 draft card itself has now been read from a Fold3 image. It gives 87 Huguenot Street, not 17, as his home and as Anna's address, and it is dated 13 September 1918. He was a chauffeur at Premium Point. The card remains a probable identification, because the birthday on it, 18 April 1877, still does not match the 1874 baptism.[^hennessy-wwi-draft]

openQuestions.question: Was he born in 1874 or in 1877?
openQuestions.record: The Conahy baptism of 12 April 1874 names the same parents as his 1914 marriage. A draft card gives 18 April 1877, and the 1947 death index says he was 70, which agrees with about 1877. New York death certificate 38983 (not ordered; it would need a yes) may name an age, parents and an informant.

April 1877 an, und der Sterbeindex von 1947 sagt, er sei 70 gewesen, was mit etwa 1877 übereinstimmt. Die Sterbeurkunde von New York 38983 (nicht bestellt; es wäre ein Ja nötig) kann ein Alter, Eltern und eine Auskunftsperson nennen.
